This inner component, if it exists, would be responsible for its high surface brightness and possibly its morphological features, while its outer parts would consist of a relatively thin, low-mass disk, explaining its faint surface brightness properties.

For a quasiregular self-map in 3D space, research has demonstrated that the Hausdorff dimension of its fast escaping set can be any value within the range of 1 to 3. An estimated lower bound has also been proposed for the Hausdorff dimension of its Julia set under a specific growth constraint.

Using the neutral density and vertical wind speed from MGS, ODY, MRO, and MAVEN, scientists analyzed the global distribution and propagation of gravity waves in the Mars atmosphere. The study found that MGS detected more GWs than ODY, primarily because MGS detected more waves in the northern hemisphere during its mission due to the 11-year orbital period of the two spacecraft and the 8-year Martian year. Moreover, MGS detected more GWs in the equatorial and southern hemisphere due to its higher sampling rate and the higher altitude of its detection. In contrast, MRO and MAVEN showed similar results in the equatorial and southern hemisphere since their detection started after MGS and ODY mission ended. Moreover, the four instruments found that Northern, Southern, and Equatorial regions display distinct characteristics. Specifically, the high-latitude regions display seasonal variations, while GWs in the equatorial region tend to persist throughout the mission. Moreover, the equatorial and high-latitude regions display prominent variations in the equatorial and polar regions, respectively. Moreover, the equatorial and polar regions display different day-night patterns, whereas the equatorial and high-latitude regions display distinct characteristics. Moreover, the equatorial and polar regions display distinct features, while the equatorial and high-laction regions display distinct features. Moreover, the equatorial and polar regions display distinct features, while the equatorial and high-laction regions display distinct features.

The LHC holds the record for the highest energy particle collisions, encompassing a vast spectrum from heavy ion collisions at 5.02 TeV to proton-proton encounters at 13.6 TeV. This diverse range allows the study of QCD under both high and extreme conditions. Specifically, forward J/psi production in lead-lead ultra-peripheral collisions can reveal insights into the nuclear dependence of gluon density in the forward region. Our analysis focuses on ALICE measurements of J/psi photons and J/psi distributions in lead-lead and proton-lead collisions, obtained via the reconstruction of dimuon decays. These measurements obtained in 2015 and 2016 show distinct transverse momentum distributions and production rates differing based on collision types. Notably, J/psi production in lead-pear collisions exceeds expectations based on proton-proton collisions, especially at higher energies and lower momentum levels. This discrepancy highlights the distinct characteristics of ultra-peripheral lead-lead collisions.

Recent advancements in audio generation through visual stimuli introduce an intriguing yet complex challenge. In contrast to visual content through visual images, generating sound that accurately reflects non-trivial class characteristics proves difficult. The generated sound is often plagued by inconsistencies and irregularities. The primary obstacles are the redundant nature of audio signal information and the low entropy of audio categories, both of which make the generation sound difficult. The existing models lack the ability to produce high-quality, coherent audio. In order to tackle these challenges, we've proposed a novel multi-objective generation sound approach called SOFG, grounded in a novel non-conditional latent variable model. The model's architecture allows for the direct correlation between visual images and the generation sound. Furthermore, we've refined the generation sound through a novel, non-auditory module. The model is optimized through multiple objective functions, including entropy and spectral analysis, to improve the generated sound. The proposed model outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in terms of coherence, entropy, and overall audio fidelity.

Recurrent neural networks have emerged as a highly effective architecture for processing sequential data, yet designing optimal solutions remains a persistent challenge. In our research, we investigate the capabilities of Elman's recurrent neural networks in capturing temporal information in artificial learning tasks. We establish a theoretical framework, demonstrating that Elman's recurrent networks can effectively learn and represent synthetic artificial tasks involving time-based information. Empirical tests were conducted using the letter data, showing that Elman's recurrent networks achieved near-optimal accuracy in mimicking the target stochastic mappings. Building upon this foundation, we developed a theoretical criterion, the recurrent rank, to analyze and compare the structural properties of recurrent weights in Elman's models. This analysis led to the development of a method, the time-unfolding recurrent structure, for efficiently modeling the optimal temporal representations in artificial learning tasks. Furthermore, we explored the impact of recurrent structure learning on the recurrence of hidden states, discovering a trade-off between recurrence and predictive performance.

Achieving a balance between pandemic control and economic considerations is a delicate task, as modeling under specific economic assumptions often yields non-transferable results. This research investigates how implementing timely moderate measures can resolve the trade-off between medical efficacy and economic impact, and attributes this finding to the broader concept of 'economic irreversibility,' illustrating its analogy to the principles of thermodynamics.

The objective of data debugging is to pinpoint inaccuracies and biases within training datasets that are impacting machine learning models. Our proposed method, DataShap, utilizes Shapley values to ascertain the relative significance of individual data samples in machine learning pipelines. By doing so, DataShap not only identifies specific data samples that require attention but also breaks down the influence of each data sample across various stages of the pipeline. We also integrate DataShap with active learning to accelerate the process of improving machine learning pipelines. Our data debugging approach has been tested on a collection of 26 data samples, encompassing 312 individual data instances, and achieved a 14% enhancement in classification accuracy, requiring approximately 300 fewer labeling efforts. Furthermore, the Shapley-based importance scores generated by DataShap provide pipeline developers with valuable insights into how individual data samples affect model performance, thus enabling more efficient training and improved transparency.

This work reveals underlying relationships between various, seemingly unrelated branches of mathematics: combinatorics, algebraic statistics, topology, and enumerative algebraic geometry. We emphasize discrete invariants, which have strong ties to the concept of Lorentzian polynomials. A common thread among these fields lies in a linear space of matrices.

This study provides an in-depth examination of how pressure influences the anomalous Hall effect in Mn$_3$Sn, an antiferromagnetic compound with a triangular structure. Experimental results indicate that pressure can effectively alter the magnetic properties of Mn$_3$Sn, leading to both structural and magnetic phase transitions. Notably, the magnitude of the anomalous Hall effect reaches its maximum at the point where the material loses its long-range magnetic order, suggesting that local magnetic arrangements are critical in generating the anomalous Hall effect. The observed variation in the anomalous Hall effect under pressure was quantified, and predictions suggest that pressing Mn$_3$Sn with a 1 GPa is sufficient to induce a 100% phase change. These findings imply that applying pressure can substantially enhance the performance of spintronionic devices based on Mn$_3$Sn.

Formal knowledge acquisition is pivotal for developing artificial intelligence systems capable of understanding, inference, and logical reasoning. A critical initial step towards this goal involves extracting relational information from semi-structured and unstructured data sources such as databases, tables, and natural language texts. A particularly challenging aspect of this goal lies in relation extraction from natural language texts. Despite significant advancements, this task remains unsolved due to the ambiguity and complexity of human language. The primary difficulty lies in accurately identifying and categorizing relations and their associated entities within the given text. This article provides an in-depth analysis of recent approaches to relation extraction and their underlying methodologies, along with an examination of their performance in various relation extraction tasks. Additionally, this article discusses open issues, potential research directions, and limitations of current approaches, along with proposing potential solutions.

This paper delves into a Steklov-Robin eigenvalue problem for the Laplacian in a particular class of annular domains. Specifically, we examine a setup involving a larger open set $\Omega_0$ and a smaller compact subdomain $\Omega\subsetneq \Omega_0$ with a smooth boundary. Within this setup, we consider a part of the boundary, $\Gamma$, and its complement $\Gamma^c$. Our goal is to find the Steklov-Robin eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, subject to certain boundary conditions on both $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^c$. 

To study the asymptotic behavior of these eigenvalues, we introduce a family of annular domains and make some reasonable assumptions about the geometry of $\Omega$. Upon investigating the eigenvalue problem, we discover the existence of infinitely many Dirichlet-Neumann eigenvalues that converge to infinity. Notably, the associated eigenvectors exhibit exponential localization towards the inner boundary $\Gamma$.

We investigate a widely used but theoretically complex method: reconstructing a hypergraph from its sampled node and edge counts. The application of machine learning principles to this problem is explored. In linear and radial free energy scenarios, optimal edge sample allocation is identified, and it's confirmed that given sufficient edges, optimal sampling achieves the best rate of edge count estimation. When linear assumptions prevail, this rate is equivalent to that of estimating the corresponding degree sequence, whereas under radial assumptions, it surpasses this benchmark. However, in all other scenarios, this benchmark is unattainable. When edge samples are limited, both edge and degree sequence estimation are found to be infeasible beyond certain thresholds. In particular, edge recovery proves more challenging, requiring more than twice the threshold amount of samples.

In medical radiology reports, doctors document vital information about patients'
health conditions. Their findings are derived from analyzing imaging tools, 
including chest X-Rays. Annotating chest X-Rays with rudimentary elements 
like bones and organs hampers radiologists' ability to read them. Our solution 
involves developing a novel annotation system, which leverages Computed Tomography
data to produce precise 2D annotations. These annotations align with the original
images and address issues resulting from patient movement. Furthermore, our 
annotations serve as a foundation for advanced annotated datasets and models, 
as well as customized annotation tools for researchers and clinicians working 
with medical imaging data. The source code, along with sample datasets and tools,
can be accessed via the provided link.

Bill Thurston initially found that Euler classes of taut foliations in hyperbolic 3-manifolds have a limited range and then made an educated guess that this range is the absolute minimum. Subsequent work by a different researcher, collaborating with David Gabai, found counterexamples that contradict this theory. Due to the connection between tight contact structures and taut foliations, researchers now consider that there might be other examples that contradict the original theory. To address this, researchers have developed a plan to compare Euler classes of tight contact structures with that of the universal cover, then write down the details of this plan in detail.

We propose an advanced concept for measuring directional emission in microcavity lasers. Initially, entropy in the polar far-field profile effectively gauges the degree of unidirectional light release, outperforming previous methods which struggle with variation. Secondly, we introduce a phenomenological angle for measuring emission directionality, but its practical application is limited to straightforward cases due to the inability to handle complex structures. Conversely, entropy based on semi-marginal probability in the Cartesian coordinate achieves comparable results and is also adaptable to emissions with complex structures.

Our findings indicate that the characteristics of cryptocurrencies as a payment method are fundamentally stochastic, but their stability tends to improve over longer periods, with currencies like Bitcoin showing a preferred direction of movement more than 55% of the time over exchanges with a minimum 1% price change. Whereas shorter intervals reveal no clear preference for upward or downward price movements, this stability increases for periods of one week or longer. To better understand this stability, we evaluated the suitability of well-known financial models for describing the cryptocurrency market, focusing on the distribution of returns and the frequency of observations, but these models have different levels of success in explaining the stability of Bitcoin and Ethereum due to the unique nature of their price data, which is influenced by the absence of traditional financial trading restrictions.

We formulate an explicit formula for the two-point correlation function of the KPz equation with initial conditions drawn from a Gaussian distribution. It is proven that as the noise amplitude squared approaches zero, this correlation function converges uniformly. Furthermore, we establish a non-linear analog of a limit law, similar to that found in the Burgers equation, and leveraged in weak noise theory. Utilizing the inverse scattering method, we derive a formula expressing the correlator in terms of the inverse scattering problem for the KPz solution u(t,x,y) at a specific time t and locations x,y. This formula incorporates a solution to an integral equation involving the scattering data of the KPz solution with zero initial conditions.

The solar wind's compressive plasma turbulence at sub-ion scales is analyzed with data from the Magnetospheric MultiScale mission. Utilizing various methods like spectral density, structure functions, wavelet transforms, and Hilbert transforms, we investigate turbulent characteristics. Additionally, we examine the potential for observing these compressive structures using wave forms, statistics, and 3D reconstruction techniques. However, due to the fast rotation of Earth's orbit, we struggle to distinguish between different structures, thereby challenging our understanding of sub-ion scale compressive turbulence.

In SASE FEL schemes, short pulse durations are usually achieved with low-energy electrons and short gain lengths, which limits the photon energy to low ranges. To overcome this constraint, pulse- shaping techniques like chirp-taper can be applied post-amplification to lower the pulse duration and extend the photon energy. This research demonstrates a modified chimp-taper technique that not only reduces pulse duration but also improves its energy stability. Utilizing this modified technique, we succeeded in producing extreme ultraviolet pulses as short as 70 fs at 13 eV within a 1 m undulator using 150 MeV electron beams, and generated a 6.5 fs pulse at 4 eV using 200 MeV electron beams in the same length. The proposed modified scheme has potential for application at existing facilities like LCLS, FLASH, and XFEL, as well as in proposed facilities like CXRLS and CXFFEL.

A mathematical model examining the impact of turbulence on a stratified flow is investigated, incorporating eddy coefficients that influence viscosity but neglect those affecting viscosity. In a particular limit, it's shown that a physical optics approximation can be used to simplify the examination of nonlinearity and turbulence effects, a finding that aligns with a previous discovery. Inside the boundary layer, the long-wave approximations of the geometric optics rays' profiles are analyzed. These profiles exhibit oscillatory behavior at a specific frequency, and their amplitudes are found to increase progressively with time, leading to potential breakdown of the geometric optics regime. Moreover, two distinct solutions emerge for these long-wave approximations, signaling non-uniqueness at specific frequencies, and indicating complex flow dynamics.

Election manipulation through the alteration of voting district boundaries constitutes
a long-standing issue in democracy, yet detecting it has been challenging due to
the absence of clear analytical indicators. To address this concern, we developed a
new analytical method called IsoPartition Gerrymandering Score (IPTS) that enables
the quantification of partisan bias within any district mapping system. The
IPTS was tested using 2,500 optimized district maps generated through a Markov
Chain method and another optimized districting algorithm, as well as several
real-world districting schemes in different states with varying levels of
partisan bias provided by the Partisan Biais de Districtation dataset. The results
show that our IPTS can effectively differentiate between optimized and
partisan-leaning maps, and accurately identify partisan-leaning maps in an
independent testing phase.

A novel defect detection approach for patterned fabric images is presented, addressing the limitations of traditional methods, which are ineffective due to the influence of patterns. A direction map, generated from a gradient direction operator, captures the pattern, while a non-local comparison, applied to a non-local mean low-rank matrix recovery model, isolates the defect region. This process, aided by the direction map, enhances the accuracy of defect detection, with the defect region further refined through subtraction from the low-rank matrix model. Numerical experiments, demonstrating the method's effectiveness, are conducted on self-collected image datasets, yielding impressive results, with a notable success rate in detecting defects.

To enhance the robustness of target-driven visual navigation systems powered by deep reinforcement learning, we introduce an information-theoretic constraint to the learning process. By maximizing the correlation between the agent's navigation actions and the resulting state observations, the agent learns to follow a more structured and logical policy, which in turn improves its robustness. Experimental results on challenging goals demonstrate that this information-theoretic regulation enhances the agent's robustness during target-driven visual navigation in real-world environments.

For asymptotically flat spacetimes, where light is emitted at a distance from the gravitational source, research indicates that the Bondi mass aspect must satisfy specific requirements to reach the point of infinity without obstruction. In the case of charged particles, such as a Reissner-Nordstrom black hole, new findings demonstrate how the rate of mass loss is limited by the balance between electric charge and the initial mass. In the case of neutral particles, these results suggest that the rate of mass loss is limited by the initial mass, regardless of other factors such as angular momentum, providing support for previous conjectures that proposed specific mass loss limits involving these components.

We've investigated the formation of Population III binary remnants within nuclear star clusters using a sophisticated simulation. These clusters form at the heart of massive galaxies, where the initial Population III stars and supermassive black holes are located, due to the collapse of the first protogalaxies. A novel star-remnant interaction, termed 'second generation hardening', emerges when population III binaries capture forming black holes through 'bouncing', giving rise to 'P-III-remnant' sources of gravitational waves. These binaries, composed of the initial population III black holes, merge within the cluster's central 10 parsecs, accounting for the majority of the detected waves by LIGO. Their associated stars, however, often get destroyed in the process, which can be seen as 'P-III-remnant' sources distinguishing themselves from the standard 'remnant' sources. These specialized wave sources offer potential new insights into the initial population III binaries residing in the central black holes of the galaxies.

In modern power distribution networks equipped with energy storage systems (ESS) and advanced control systems, the standard monitoring and protection systems are not optimized for identifying malfunctions in smart devices. This work presents a data-driven method for identifying incidents related to Power Peakers, a type of advanced control system, in distribution networks. Our approach uses measurements from phasor units and treats incident detection as a classification problem, relying on non-linear support vector machines. A simulation of a real-world real-peaker outage and field data from another actual incident are utilized to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that this method successfully detects Peaker malfunctions within 0.5 seconds with high accuracy, specifically 99.8%.

Our study focuses on how the $\rho$ and $c$ mesons contribute to the radiative decays of the $X(3872)$, and we also examine the role of gauge invariance in these processes. The calculations show that both a $\rho$-photon and a photon from the $c$-quark can participate in the decay $X(3872) \rightarrow J/\psi \pi \gamma$, but their effects cancel each other out, a common characteristic of quark-model vector resonances. However, the effects do not cancel in the four-body decay $X(3872) \rightarrow J/\psi \pi\pi \gamma$, where the $\rho$-photon contribution dominates. The differential widths of these decays are calculated and compared with existing experimental data, allowing for constraints to be placed on the coupling between $X(3872)$, $J/\psi$, and a photon. The coupling is found to be approximately 1 eV.

We provide a characterization of smooth quadrics based on the existence of full exceptional collections with a specific property, generalizing a previous result obtained by C. Vial for projective spaces.

Text-based games provide a rigorous platform to assess virtual agents in tasks like natural language understanding, solving complex problems, and applying real-world knowledge.
One significant limitation of existing text-based games is their slow speed, amounting to around 10 steps per second, which becomes a major bottleneck for comprehensive testing and fine-tuning machine learning models.
Our proposed solution, TextWorldExpress, upgrades existing text-based games by employing computational enhancements to drive simulations at up to 12,000 steps per second, facilitating large-scale simulations.
By leveraging these enhancements, we can design new and challenging game levels, and ultimately create complex training tasks that exceed the current game levels' difficulty.
Our experiments demonstrate the substantial improvements made to simulation speeds and show that Text-based games now can be run in parallel using standard hardware, and it is also possible to simulate entire training processes of large language models at realistic timescales, and it is possible to design complex tasks that are beyond the scope of existing text-based games.

The study on varying electron spin orientation employs the coordinate transformation method. Characteristic energy functions, derived for a spatial coordinate change, preserve the topological insulator's boundary surface properties. A geometric approach is used to define and differentiate between regular and defective boundary surfaces, with results verified through numerical analysis of the effective magnetic field's spin vector distribution.

Using a joint multivariate spatial model based on the work of Heffernan and Tawn, the relationship between satellite wind speed data, wave height, and extreme ocean swells is examined in three case studies from New Zealand's east coast. A standard approach is used initially but found to be limited in capturing the nature of these extremes. The model parameters were adjusted to better reflect the observed extremes, and standard models failed to accurately capture them.

Inspired by intermediate Lang conjectures concerning hyperbolicity and rational points, we establish new theorems on the finiteness of non-constant morphism sets from a specific fixed variety to another, also defined over a specific number field, by adapting Faltings's work on the finiteness of maps in moduli spaces.

A key concept in modern robotic manipulation, the manipulability ellipse, effectively represents the robot's interaction capabilities in 3D space and has numerous applications, including teaching robots new movements, simulating human movements, and guiding robotic planning. Most research on using manipulability ellipses focuses on models with 6-DoF arms. However, advancing to robots with 7-DoF arms presents challenges due to the additional joint, which significantly impacts the robot's movement capabilities. Existing methods for adapting manipulability ellipses from human to robot models are typically limited to 6-DoF robots. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach to transfer manipulability ellipses from human hands to 7-DoF robots. We do this by using the manipulability ellipse's geometric properties to represent it as a 3D object. Then, we employ a novel method to transform this object, take its joint position data, and match it with the robot's geometry using an improved iterative closest point algorithm. Our approach enables us to accurately represent the manipulability ellipse in the robot's space, which has potential applications in movement transfer and movement simulation. We've validated the effectiveness of our method through experiments on a Tuatra robot.

To study non-resonant Higgs boson pair production in the $\textrm{HH} \to
\textrm{W}\textrm{W}^{*}$ final state with at least one Higgs boson decaying into $\textrm{b}\textrm{b}$, the matrix element method is applied. 
Utilizing final state particle momenta, the production and decay of Higgs boson pairs are distinct from each other using matrix elements. 
Both signal and background processes are analyzed at the LHC at 13 TeV, considering final states with zero or one neutrinos. 
Effective fields, specifically $\textrm{SM} \times \textrm{H}^2$ and $\textrm{S}^2 \times
\textrm{J}^0\textrm{J}^0\textrm{J}^0\textrm{J}^0$, are used to calculate the signal contributions in terms of the VBF, WW, and Higgs boson mediated processes. 
For a 35 fb$^{-1}$ luminosity dataset, the signal sensitivity for the coupling $\lambda_2$ is determined to be $\pm 0.25 \times 10^4$ GeV$^{-4}$. 
The impact of background subtraction on $\lambda_2$ sensitivity is also studied with different background-to-signal ratios ($

A novel method is introduced for training single-view 3D object pose estimation models, utilizing uncurated, multi-view, in-the-wild image datasets. These models are instructed using images of objects captured in everyday settings, where objects are frequently found rotating on surfaces. The novel approach relies solely on videos of these rotating objects, obtained from uncurated datasets, without requiring labeled 3D data. A simple filtering process is applied to extract views of rotating objects, which are then used to train a method for determining the object's orientation within the camera frame. This information is leveraged to create a dataset with 3D image views, where one view aligns with the object's axis of rotation. This dataset is used to train state-of-the-art models for 3D pose estimation, outperforming previous benchmarks on various datasets. Additionally, an open dataset of rotating objects is made available to support this research at https://github.com/renliang/accidental_turntables.

Despite widespread scientific consensus on the efficacy and safety of COVID-19 vaccines, a significant portion of the population remains hesitant to get vaccinated. Malicious actors have exploited social media platforms to disseminate vaccine disinformation, which has posed a major challenge. While existing research has focused on analyzing the impact of such misinformation, relatively little is known about how platforms like Twitter regulate the adoption or rejection of such misinformation within community discussions. By using large-scale data from Twitter related to COVID-19 vaccines, our study investigated the behaviors of users who post misinformation, as well as how such misinformation is perceived and regulated during community discussions. Our analysis revealed that misinformation targeters receive a significant disparity in responses from users who validate versus reject such misinformation. Furthermore, our results show that users who validate such misinformation tend to express stronger personal beliefs and emphasize sources of such misinformation, while rejecting such misinformation, on the other hand, often involves users engaging in conversations with sources of such misinformation, as well as emphasizing scientific knowledge, personal experiences, and a consensus of such misinformation. Our findings provide insights for misinformation targeters, validation, and rejection within the context of Twitter discussions and highlight a potential gap between the Facebook Misinformation Targeters and Machine Learning Challenge in terms of semantic similarity metrics.

Advancements in attosecond science hold great potential for resolving rapid electron dynamics outside of light's confinement. In our approach, a highly intense, short pulse is produced using the combination of two near-infrared femtosecond laser pulses and an optimal multilayer metal structure. The interaction of this structure with the laser generates an attosecond burst with a duration of less than 100 fs. We demonstrate that adjusting the relative phase and polarization of the two laser pulses enables us to precisely control the attosecond pulse's intensity and temporal characteristics, offering a new method for achieving strong-field coherent control at the atomic scale.

Eclipse predictions for binary systems can be significantly improved by incorporating fresh data from spectroscopic studies. In this research, spectroscopic observations of the Algol binary system AB were conducted over a period of 16 years, yielding crucial findings. Notably, the analysis revealed the presence of two previously undetected companion candidates, which prompted a re-evaluation of the system's geometry. It was discovered that the companion candidates have contributed to the shortening of the binary system AB's orbital period. Furthermore, it was found that the current eclipse predictions are highly accurate, with a remaining margin of only 37.5 minutes.

This paper investigates solutions to the Schrödinger equation under the influence of a focusing nonlinearity with mass-supercritical properties, in a domain exterior to a compact convex obstacle. We demonstrate that solutions will eventually become unbounded within a finite time, specifically for initial conditions that meet certain energy and mass criteria, and are localized outside the obstacle's shadow region. These results generalize existing findings by the authors and others, which previously established that solutions would blow finite time in the whole space scenario, under analogous conditions.

Physics-informed neural networks offer an innovative solution for partial differential equations that combines adaptability and efficient incorporation of observed data. Despite achieving significant success across a wide array of differential equations, further improvements can be made by enhancing data point selection and solution training. To address this need, our proposed Residual-based Adaptive Node Generation method optimizes the position of data points and training times based on the local error. By dynamically producing data points in areas of high local error, we maximize adaptation and sampling efficiency. Numerical experiments demonstrate the method's ability to deliver superior results with fewer data points, and outperform both standard Physics-informed neural networks and other error-controlled approaches.

This study examines the behavior and simulation of multi-domain ferroelectric FETs by analyzing the oscillations in their electrostatic conduction bands, which are characterized by negative capacitance. These fluctuations, observed in experiments, are crucial for understanding the time-based operations of these devices, particularly in systems featuring a domain wall. By solving the time-dependent Poisson's equation, we have discovered that negative capacitance is a direct result of the wavy electrostatic conduction band, whose magnitude is controlled by the domain wall. Furthermore, the magnitude of this phenomenon increases as the domain wall approaches the channel center, as evidenced by our simulations.

A study of software vulnerabilities reveals that researchers lack clarity on how vulnerabilities spread within software projects, particularly in terms of whether and how a vulnerability propagates during dependencies updates. An analysis of the Java ecosystem shows that nearly 40% of dependencies propagate vulnerabilities, with the majority causing low-severity issues. When projects depend on updated dependencies that introduce vulnerabilities, the severity tends to increase. A novel dependency-vulnerability knowledge graph has been proposed to facilitate the discovery of hidden ecosystem vulnerabilities, demonstrating its efficacy in finding previously unknown vulnerabilities. Additionally, to gauge the effect of software vulnerabilities on damage, a model has been developed that shows how vulnerabilities in open-source projects could lead to service disruptions, downtime, and financial losses.

For analyzing ergodic properties in stochastic dynamical systems, it's essential to demonstrate irreducibility. This paper confirms the irreducibility of stochastic complex Ginzburg-Landau equations subjected to discrete jump noises and shows these results apply universally, imposing minimal restrictions on noise conditions. Notably, this outcome contrasts with results for stochastic systems with continuous noises; specifically, ensuring irreducibility in the latter requires ensuring the noise's ellipticity, whereas our proof for the discrete case does not require such strict prerequisites.

For a finite noncyclic nilpotent group G, we're analyzing the minimal vertex degree in its power graph. This power graph connects vertices based on one being a positive power of the other. By examining the group's prime divisors and Sylow subgroups, we've pinpointed vertices related to its cyclic subgroups. This allows us to establish a connection between the group's properties and its minimal vertex degree in the power graph. This study provides degree calculations for specific types of noncyclic abelian groups.

Hadron-hadron collisions in the intermediate Feynman-x region (between 0.1 and 0.9) have not been extensively studied at high-energy ranges above sqrt(s) = 63 GeV using the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings. I explore the feasibility of a high-energy experiment that could shed light on this unknown territory. Considering that such collisions may provide crucial insights into understanding the behavior of cosmic ray particles at the highest energy levels.

Deep learning models, specifically Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs), are capable of generating robust image representations, but are limited when dealing with orientation transformations. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel model class, Orientation Convolution Networks (OCNs), which are an extension of DCNNs that preserve rotation symmetry. By orienting filters in OCNs, distinct features are extracted by these filters, and a set of weighted fusion filters is designed to converge to invariant filters. This design enables OCNs to assume rotation invariant properties without necessitating the use of rotation-invariant datasets. Through comprehensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, the proposed model has demonstrated comparable performance to state-of-the-art DCNNs.

This study seeks to enhance the computational efficiency of graph convolutional networks (GCNs) for 3D point cloud processing by investigating the effects of graph convolution, a critical graph neural network (GNN) component often overlooked in the current literature. Our analysis reveals that for common point cloud processing, GCPs yield superior geometric feature representations over other graph operations, such as graph pooling and residual networks, and can even surpass them in GCN performance. Furthermore, based on the assumptions made during graph convolution and the resulting output, we found that these assumptions hold true for point cloud processing, enabling the development of more efficient GCNs. Specifically, we propose two alternatives to GCNs: GPCoat, which omits the output offset vector without significant performance loss, and GPCat, which replaces graph convolution with element-wise multiplication between input data and output vectors, a simpler operation that entails no performance decline. Our proposed architectures demonstrate superior computational efficiency while maintaining comparable representation capabilities to existing GCNs.

We introduce a groundbreaking type of Trojan attack, which uses meaning-based instructions to control its activation, independent of the host network. Unlike existing Trojan attacks, which manipulate images to trigger abnormal behavior, our approach creates authentic audio-visual content by utilizing normal, everyday phrases. Specifically, we use the audio-visual dataset AudioActive to develop Semantic Host-Free Audio-Visual Trojans that recognize and respond to predefined, meaning-based sound cues. Our type of Trojan attack is distinct as it targets a combination of sound and image input, and its creation and activation are governed by a model that accounts for both modality's contributions. Experimental findings show that our Semantic Host-Free Trojan attack is exceptionally difficult to detect, and is substantially more advanced than the existing state-of-theart Trojan attack.

We are developing an image slicer for the ROSIE integral field unit, to be installed on the IMACS spectrograph at the Magellan Telescope. This integral field unit will feature a low-resolution, cross-dispersed spectrograph with 256 simultaneous 2D spectral fields. Each field will capture a 0.4 arcsec x 6.4 arcsec chunk of the sky, and be dispersed at 1.5 micron with 2000 per micron arcsec resolution. The unit's optical design employs two grating approaches for different wavelength ranges.

In this paper, the carbon-carbon fusion research is revisited to incorporate the latest developments. Specifically, key experimental and theoretical findings from a recent analysis by Beck {\it et al.} (Eur. Phys. J. A {\bf 53}, 19, 2017) are considered to outline the pathway for enhancing low-energy astrophysical $S$-factor determinations via new Threshold Hand Mirror (THM) measurements.

A crucial aspect of discovering and studying exoplanets is identifying terrestrial planets similar to Earth. New studies focus on the significance of planetary compositions, which can offer insights into the formation and development of these planets. Research indicates that factors like elemental abundances, particularly volatile elements, influence the composition of planets, but other components like magnesium and silicon also play a role. This research delves into how planetary compositions are affected by stellar metallicity, magnesium, and silicon for three types of minerals: olivine, pyroxene, and spinel. By applying numerical models, the study provides precise calculations for planetary mantle viscosity, melting points, crust thickness, and the time required to form continental masses, based on stellar metallicity. Additionally, the work offers an analytical framework for predicting mineralogical compositions of silicates, expanding previous research that focused solely on magnesium and silicon in stellar environments. This framework can be used for any elemental distribution following atomic order, following iron, nickel, and cobalt. Furthermore, the study presents magnesium and silicon distribution laws for planetary bodies, which can be used for terrestrial exoplanets and may have implications for spectroscopy in astronomical observations.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become a preferred method for wireless localization due to their ability to utilize raw channel measurements, circumventing the limitations of traditional techniques that rely on specific channel parameters. Nevertheless, the success of DNN-based localization is hindered in indoor environments, characterized by low direct line-of-sight components and significant multipath effects. Our research aims to overcome this challenge, focusing on a narrow-band cognitive radio system with a direct and obstructed path (COP/EOP) configuration. Our innovation lies in the proposal of an attention-based model, which leverages a data-driven approach to differentiate and weigh critical environmental characteristics, thereby optimizing performance. Our experiments, conducted over the air using an software-defined radio platform, demonstrate that the attention-based model surpasses a conventional d-dimensional wireless localization system (WDLS) in several key evaluation metrics.

This paper presents a comprehensive framework for modal logic semantics by linking different types of logical meaning in the literature to the topological categories theory. Building on similar methods in categorical logic, we will thoroughly examine the relationship between the structural composition of the modal language, its various expansions, and the topological structures in categories, thus offering an abstract understanding of the underlying logical framework.

A graph's edge coloring can be described as assigning different colors to edges based on a specific distance criterion, effectively mirroring the requirements of a certain vertex coloring in a transformed version of the graph. This notion was initially proposed as an open problem by Faudree, Schelp, Gyárfás, and Tuza in 1990, assuming a bipartite graph of high enough girth and a specific degree configuration would be colored using a specific number of colors, but the validity of this claim remains unresolved for over two decades. In this paper, we present a counterexample, taking the form of a bipartite cube, which features 24 vertices and 7 colors in its edge coloring. This discovered exception prompts the need for the development of a general theory and rules to guide the edge coloring process in cubic graphs, especially those with a particular structural characteristic, known as being 3-vertex connected.

We investigate functions defined on the vertices of the Hamming graphs H(n,q), focusing specifically on those with support contained within the union of complete parts formed by the distance from a starting point. Let's consider functions f belonging to the direct sum of complete parts, denoted as $P_0^0(d_0) \oplus \ldots \oplus P_0^0(d_{n-1})$. Our research demonstrates that if the size of the function's support is below a calculated limit tied with the dimensions n and q, then f is zero. This calculated limit is verified when n equals q minus one or two, where it matches the gugger number of the Hamming graph H(n,q). We will discuss the implications of this result in relation to the Levenshtein bounds for binary codes, particularly those with specific Krawchouk coefficients.

COPASI is a widely-used simulation and analysis tool for biochemical networks. It offers various built-in analysis techniques, yet integrating them into a user-friendly, interactive framework is not a straightforward process. One key feature of COPASI is its capability to create custom graphical representations, which can be utilized in applications like generating dynamic reaction equations or creating phase-plane diagrams. However, accessing these capabilities within the desktop-based COPASI can be challenging due to limitations in its built-in graphing library. To overcome this limitation, we have developed ShinyCOPASI, a web-based interface that allows users to perform various COPASI analysis techniques and utilize COPASI graphs in this way.

Deep neural networks are increasingly relied upon in Domain-specific Deep Learning (SDL) for predicting outcomes of complex physical or chemical simulations. Nevertheless, neural network predictions are inherently uncertain, underscoring the need to quantify this uncertainty in high-stakes domains. The role of uncertainty quantification in SDL is still emerging, so we aim to clarify this important topic by defining key concepts and definitions associated with it. Furthermore, we will introduce and explain performance measures used to assess uncertainty quantification accuracy, which will facilitate future research focused on validating and verifying uncertainty quantification. Ultimately, this note serves as a comparative analysis of various uncertainty quantification techniques, allowing researchers to choose the method that best fits their specific application and setting.

We investigate quantum analogs of the von Neumann algebras related to class functions on compact quantum groups. Specifically, for the free quantum permutation group, we demonstrate that this analog is finite-dimensional, and for supergroups, it corresponds to the Gelfand-Naimark algebra. Additionally, we establish criteria under which class function algebras for permutation groups are simple and determine their dimension. Furthermore, we compute this algebra directly for linear Hahn quantum groups and establish its properties. Lastly, we identify key features for class function algebras across various quantum groups, including dimensional constraints and the absence of quantum analogs for direct products.

Policy iteration comes with computational drawbacks in large-scale Markov decision processes due to a local quadratic contraction rate and the costliness of value iteration's policy evaluation (PE) step. Researchers have proposed inexact policy iteration (IPi), which incorporates an inner loop of approximate value iterations to accelerate convergence. A key property of IPi is its local linear contraction rate, which reduces the number of value iterations as it approaches the optimal solution. This paper focuses on a modification of the policy iteration with approximate policy evaluation (PI-APE) approach, where the policy evaluation is performed using Generalized Minimal Residual iterations (GMRES), a standard iterative solver. We examine the convergence of the new algorithm, where the Peaceman-Ruppel and Saad-Yang modifications to GMRES are either employed or avoided, respectively. Notably, the analysis reveals a novel connection between the GMRES norm and the $L_1$-norm in the context of Markov decision processes.

Consider a weighted directed graph, denoted as $\mathcal{D}$, and the edge ideal associated with it, labeled as $I(\mathcal{D})$. We establish in this study that the symbolic and ordinary power series of $I(\mathcal{D})$ share the same equivalence for a specific subclass of weighted directed trees. Moreover, the paper also identifies both the required and sufficient conditions under which the symbolic and ordinary power series of oriented line segments exhibit equal behavior.

This paper explores a method to estimate a time-based input parameter for a virtual experiment under fixed conditions, where reducing the difference between the simulated and observed data is the primary objective. To achieve this, we propose simultaneously tracking the optimal parameter estimates for each time point of the observed data, using a multi-objective optimization approach. Our proposed method combines the Bayesian approach and the Nested Sampling algorithm, enabling efficient tracking of optimal solutions across the time series. To demonstrate the tracking process, we compare two Bayesian estimators – one based on the Maximum Entropy method and another derived from the variational inference framework. Our novel approach allows for efficient evaluation of the tracking progress at each time step, avoiding issues with local minima. Two case studies are provided to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

Research has demonstrated that certain compression techniques are capable of robustly learning simple tasks, such as balanced distributions, even in the presence of significant noise levels. Notably, these approaches rely on local queries, specifically gradient evaluation, which are not permitted in the standard robust learning model. In contrast, our investigation focuses on single-source noise and investigates the utility of local queries in the context of more complex data structures. Our research focuses on two key aspects: first, we establish a noise-resilient learning approach for intersection models of basic geometric shapes in higher dimensions, such as half-spaces or Euclidean balls, which were previously proven to be efficiently learnable even under extreme noise levels. Furthermore, our research complements existing proofs showing certain complexity constraints that prevent efficient noise-resilient learning for these geometric models. Additionally, our research explores the query complexity barrier in the local query model for efficiently noise-resilient learning intersection models of Euclidean balls. Lastly, our research presents an alternative approach to proving certain constraints that prevent robust learning for half-spaces, which is based on the concept of local queries.

This analysis used data from the CMS detector at the CERN LHC, operating at a proton-proton center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV. The fragmentation functions for jets above 30 GeV were determined and compared in the presence of a high-density medium, formed during these collisions, with those in a less dense proton-proton environment. Recent research involving Feynman integrals has highlighted the significance of Apéry-type inverse binomial series. Building upon previous findings that non-alternating central binomial series could be solved using level four multiple zeta values, we now show that alternating versions require level eight. We derive novel identities by expressing both alternating and nonalternating series in terms of both 11ary and 10ary multiple zeta values. Our analysis reveals that the series' values can be represented using colored multiple zeta values, specifically those of level four and eight.

Recent data from the NACO/ADONIS instrument at ESO's Paranal Observatory, along with parallax information from the Gaia DR2 database, allow us to analyze the motion of a peculiar brown dwarf located in the Milky Way. It took nearly two decades for researchers to discover that this object is actually on a highly elliptical orbit with a 3.7 billion year period, resulting from an encounter with another brown dwarf. This unusual encounter caused the object to take a detour, increasing its distance from the center of the galaxy by 13.6 parsecs and 20 parsecs transverse to its path. This brown dwarf, known as WISEA J153429.75-104303.3 and also called BOV Centauri A, is on a journey that will bring it back to its original plane in about 170,000 years and will add about 130 parsecs to its orbit around the center of the galaxy when it finally completes another cycle.

The initial production measurement of various particles such as pions, kaons, 
protons and $\phi$ mesons in midrapidity for the Xe-Xe collision system at 
$E_{\rm beam} = 5.44$ TeV is presented. This is the first time that 
invariant spectra and nuclear modification factors for the midrapidity region are 
calculated for protons and $\phi$ mesons in Xe-Xe collisions. Data are also 
compared to the Pb-Pb collision system and protons in p-Pb collisions. 
Results show that the multiplicity per unit rapidity and transverse momentum 
distributions in Xe-Xe collisions exceed those in Pb-Pb collisions at the same 
collision energy. protons in p-Pb collisions. Data exhibit characteristics 
consistent with the CERN Antiproton, Slow Neutron and Synchrotron (PAS) 
system exhibiting collective behavior already in small nuclei. Data exhibit 
collective behavior in the presence of a considerable magnetic field.

We develop a novel, numerically efficient approach to solving DGLAP equations for single and double parton distribution functions by leveraging Chebyshev interpolation techniques. This method enhances numerical precision with a reduced number of grid points for PDF evolution, achieving improved efficiency. The DPD evolution process utilizes a cost-effective grid-point scheme, enabling the incorporation of two distinct renormalization scales for each parton. The proposed methods account for NNLO DGLAP kernels and flavor matching.

Space exploration missions to destinations like the Moon and Mars face significant construction challenges due to in-situ resource availability. Research into constructing habitats using local regolith materials, for example, has just begun. This study aims to investigate the properties of built structures made from Martian, Lunar, and Martian-like soil. We examined the effect of Sintering temperatures on the mechanical and physical properties of built samples using local materials from the Mars and Moon. We found that sintering at 600°C for both Lunar and Martian samples optimizes their strength and stiffness without compromising their density. This optimal temperature results in stronger and stiffer samples without increasing their weight. We observed that both types of samples exhibit two distinct mechanical behaviors and the presence of dust minerals significantly contributes to their compressive strength. Our research suggests that sintering is a viable method for creating and strengthening built structures using both Lunar and Martian soil materials at extraterrestrial sites.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber heavily depend on the boundary conditions at the liquid-solid interface. This is particularly evident in the amplification of perturbations due to the slip enhancement of the film. By assuming the film is thin and a fiber of radius $a$ is present, we do not require the slip length to be much smaller than $a$. This allows for a linearized model of the film dynamics, which can be analyzed using asymptotic theory. Two regimes arise depending on the relative magnitude of the slip length and the film thickness. In one regime, where the slip length much exceeds the film thickness, two types of slip-enhanced behaviors are observed: (1) an increase in the growth rate of perturbations and (2) an increase in certain modes of wave propagation.

By comparing observed and predicted data for 178 star-forming galaxies from the zCLOUDS project, we assess the accuracy of star formation rate predictions made by three different spectral energy density modeling methods. This is the initial paper in a series that explores symmetries of local $\mathfrak sl_N$-modules, particularly those with finite or bounded weights, for $N$ being an integer greater than one. We make a discovery of new automorphisms, each swapping the highest and lowest weight, in addition to conventional local symmetries, for certain highest weight modules, over fields, with characteristic not equal to 2, having a bounded or finite set of weights, and weights confined within the $\mathfr sl_N$ weight lattice, respectively. We explicitly construct these automorphisms, under the condition of the field's characteristic not being equal to 2, but where this characteristic can be 2, only the identity and the standard involution exists. This allows us to identify the centralizers of the universal central extensions of the universal central covering of the Weyl group of $\mathfr sl_N$, under the action of the root lattice, for the action being defined over the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Z$. We anticipate that the automorphisms will have applications in the representation theory of infinite dimensional algebras and quantum groups.

The Fisher-KPP equation, a reaction-diffusion equation, was first introduced by Fisher for modelling allele spread within genetic populations, but also gained applications by Kolmogorov for a broader range of scenarios. Applying an innovative approach for tackling non-linear partial differential equations provides a distinctive approximate solution to the Fisher-KPP equation, which, however, defies initial intuition. Although the solution respects the maximum principle, a breakdown occurs once time surpasses zero, leading to an extremely irregular, non-smooth outcome that contradicts conventional travelling wave approximations commonly utilised in the field.

In recent years, there's been a significant surge in handwritten text recognition,
primarily driven by the need to analyze handwriting from devices like Graphing
Dynamics Calculator (GDCAS) which is equipped with sensors capable of tracking
hand movements. To address the complexity of recognizing mathematical symbols
and equations, we've developed a system that leverles machine learning
algorithms to improve recognition accuracy. This system employs feature
extraction, using hand pose recognition and dynamically changing wave patterns
derived from sensor data. Various machine learning classifiers, including Naive
Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), were
tested and compared to our initial results to explore their potential to
outperform the current approach and address the limitations of the GDCAS device.

This paper introduces an innovative method for duration modeling in statistical paralinguistic systems, based on speech samples, without requiring the estimation of a specific probability distribution. Unlike traditional approaches, this new median-duration model avoids the limitations of assuming a particular distribution, and also circumvents a well-known issue where low-frequency phoneme durations have excessive weight on distribution estimates. Instead, this model relies on a median duration, calculated independently for each phoneme, and is robust to noise and outliers. Experimental results demonstrate that this model outperforms existing distribution-based models in performance.

Species distribution analysis has been a standard approach in ecology for collecting and analyzing survey data, and the R package spOccupancy supports this by providing analysis tools for both single and multiple species studies. The spOccupancy R package facilitates the examination of species absence or non-detection data in various formats such as audio recordings, images, tabulations, continuous measurements, and other forms of presence data. Furthermore, it integrates these observations with known species locations. The package facilitates the fitting of hierarchical Bayesian spatial occupancy models using the Stan computational engine. The package also offers diagnostic tools to evaluate observed data against model predictions and provides options for predicting species absence or non-detection with the use of existing survey methods. The package also extends its capabilities to analyze species presence, absence, and integration of traditional survey methods with passive data collection methods such as environmental audio recordings and camera traps.

The Skincare project is an advanced diagnostic tool for dermatology that uses deep learning technology to analyze dermoscopic images of skin abnormalities. This innovative system supports dermatologists in making more informed decisions when diagnosing and treating patients, despite the challenges and limitations associated with its implementation. These challenges include potential legal implications, technical hurdles, and ethical concerns. The Skincare project aims to explore new possibilities in the field of dermatology by proposing interactive methods that enable human experts and the AI system to collaborate and communicate effectively. This collaborative diagnosis method has been tested and demonstrated in a controlled setting, involving dermatologists from the Hospices Civils de Geneva, in partnership with the University of Geneva's Computer Vision and Learning Research Center.

To capture the inherent complexity of supernovae data, we applied a probabilistic autoencoder to spectral information from over 500 Type Ia supernovae. This encoder serves as a versatile tool for reducing dimensionality, identifying patterns, and predicting key parameters from supernovae light curves. By incorporating an autoencoder into existing classification methods, we improved their accuracy and found that it compensates for issues caused by incomplete training sets. Furthermore, we found that the latent space generated by our model effectively distinguishes between different supernovae, and identified key features that influence their light curves.

The detection of an outgoing outflow, originating from the galaxy DW1717+2, presents an intriguing phenomenon which requires further investigation. Our observations using the NIRSPEC instrument on the VLT have allowed us to obtain a resolved spectrum, which reveals a massive, massive galaxy with significant dust and massive star formation. The continuum emission suggests the presence of a massive galaxy with significant mass, while the high-ionization [NeV] 3.02 um line confirms the existence of an outflow with significant speed of 800 km/s. This indicates the presence of an outflow driven by the radiation of the massive star population within the galaxy. The observed properties of the galaxy are consistent with the theoretical models of massive galaxies, suggesting the presence of a massive, massive galaxy with significant star formation. The detection of an outflow in this galaxy provides further evidence of the dynamic processes occurring in massive galaxies during their formative stages.

To study the movement of fluid into a swirling, turbulent plume containing heavy particles that sink slower than the fluid moves, researchers used controlled experiments in a well-mixed tank with varying particle sizes and densities. They measured the movement of fluid and the mixture of fluids, especially in areas where the plume meets the surrounding fluid. They found that when particles sink faster, there's more fluid moved into the plume due to the creation of strong waves and structures that mix the fluids. This study provides new data to understand how particles affect the movement of fluids in certain conditions that are not fully explained by existing research.

Understanding the spread of epidemics within networks, such as contact graphs, reveals that the behavior of these systems can be predicted based on the relationship between the infection rate and the second-largest eigenvalue of the Laplacian. In cases where multiple hyperedges are considered, with each having its own set of influences, the threshold appears to be linked to the same LAPLE value. However, the exact impact of infection and recovery rates across different hyperedges was previously unknown. By examining a specific type of hypergraph known as the bipartite model, where one part represents individuals and the other represents interactions, the research shows that, under certain conditions, the threshold is manageable and follows a pattern similar to traditional networks.

Recent breakthroughs in understanding 2D magnetic semiconductors, notably the observation of long-range ferromagnetic order within them, have opened up new avenues for research into their electronic, spin, and thermal transport. Research is now focusing on whether these materials exhibit intrinsic ferromagnetic semiconductor properties in their bulk form or if their properties are intrinsic to 2D ferromagnetic order. The answer to this question lies in our understanding of the spin texture within the Rashba spin polarization of their spin waves. This study predicts the existence of spin-backflow effects, observed for the first time through numerical simulations of the spin-wave functional of the Heisenberg model, at the edge of Rashba-sheared ferromagnetic bilayers, specifically the CrI3 material. It has been found that a in-plane magnetic field applied to a vacuum is incapable of producing long-range ferromagnetic order across a thin-film semiconductor. However, if the semiconductor's surfaces are placed in a vacuum with an applied in-plane magnetic field, a unique spin texture emerges at the edge, characterized by a stable k-point that represents a semimetallic Dirac point, and a specific spin alignment within magnetic bands. This alignment can be adjusted by altering the size of the crystal lattice, the bond stiffness, and the size of an applied magnetic field. The rotation of most solar-like stars slows down considerably from their birth, but how their angular velocity changes from the pole to the equator remains unclear. By incorporating a specific description of this change into mean-field dynamo models, we're able to discover that dynamic simulations can produce magnetic cycles in stars with very slow rotation, something that wasn't possible before. This achievement has significant implications for understanding the magnetic cycles of stars that aren't rotating as vigorously as our Sun.

Deep multimodal learning models have drawn significant interest due to their ability to integrate information from various sources, allowing for more accurate predictions and a deeper understanding of complex tasks. Current deep learning models are limited to processing two types of information and require extensive data to produce reliable results. This paper presents a novel approach to overcome these limitations by developing a k-fan multimodal deep model. Our model utilizes multiple pathways to process different sources of information simultaneously and shares representations across the pathways to efficiently utilize limited data. We provide a theoretical framework for representation sharing, showing that it enables the processing of complex tasks with fewer parameters. Extensive experiments on three tasks, including classification, prediction, and segmenting, demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed model, showing significant improvements over state-of-the-art techniques.

The use of model checking has become increasingly crucial in validating the correctness of single-threaded applications, yet it remains underutilized in verifying multi-threaded codes due to the complexity and scalability issues associated with its applications. Previous models and tools focused primarily on detecting specific types of errors in multithreaded codes using the Herdman-Wong order-based detection method, but they struggled with scalability. On the other hand, modern DPOR models and tools are capable of handling more complex scenarios, yet they face significant challenges in efficiently processing large workloads.

In this study, we present McMini, a novel model checker designed for verifying single- and multi-threaded codes. Built on the DPOR foundation, McMini integrates innovative techniques to improve efficiency in detecting potential race conditions and prevents false positives resulting from out-of-order executions. It efficiently manages the model checking process of both simple and complex programs by implementing on-the-fly refinement and a new time-queue management system.

Our experimental results validate the suitability of McMini as a potential replacement for model checking in validating race conditions in both single- and multi-threaded codes, showcasing its ability to effectively detect race conditions and avoid false positives. It has been further enhanced with a programming interface that enables users to easily customize its underlying verification methods to suit their specific requirements.

The global popularity of WhatsApp has somehow given rise to a problem, where it is frequently utilized to disseminate false information due to its features that allow unrestricted message sharing among group members. The misinformation spread via WhatsApp has severe implications on public health policy and the local economy. In 2018, WhatsApp introduced the "Forward Limit" feature to mitigate the rapid dissemination of inaccurate data. This study evaluates the effectiveness of this change by examining the forward limits imposed in India and their impact on false information propagation related to healthcare and other critical topics. Our statistical analysis, based on text and graph analytics, demonstrates that the Forward Limit feature substantially curtails message sharing and imposes significant disparities in message propagation patterns before and after its implementation. The effect of this feature on misinformation propagation is pronounced and leads to a substantial decrease in average forward rates and potential reaches. Our findings also show that the Forward Limit feature exacerbates public health misinformation and reveals distinct disparities in message forwarding patterns among country's top ten most popular communities and the top fifty commonly shared posts.

We analyze a general branching population where individual lifetimes are independent and identically distributed with arbitrary distributions, and individuals give birth to new ones at random times following a Poisson process independently from each other. It's assumed that individuals have different alleles according to a discrete distribution, and we derive an exact formula for the distribution of alleles in the population at a given time. This formula can be approximated in two scenarios: one where the population size grows slowly and another where it increases rapidly. These approximations are then applied to specific population models, and their statistical implications are discussed.

The primary goal of our spoofing countermeasure system is to identify artificial effects within spoken input that arise from speech synthesis or voice alteration techniques. We achieve this goal by incorporating a specialized, attentive activation function - the attention rectified linear unit (AReLU) - into our end-to-end system. By selectively amplifying key input characteristics and suppressing irrelevant ones, AReLU enables our system to prioritize artifact-related features. Our proposed system was evaluated using the popular OWSC-19 dataset and demonstrated superior performance compared to baseline methods, with EER rates of 13.71%, 19.78%, and 14.74% across different deep neural network variants.

Supergravity, an extension of the Standard Model with local supersymmetry, may offer a more comprehensive model of fundamental physics. This suggests that supergravity could provide a more complete description of the cosmic inflation process. This review focuses on supergravity-based cosmological models, with a particular emphasis on those incorporating de Sitter effective field theories to describe the inflationary phase. These models are characterized by four key parameters: superpotential magnitude, Giudice-Masiero term magnitude, non-minimal kinetic term coefficient, and non-zero eigenvalue of the mass matrix's zero-mode spectrum. We explore conditions for achieving these models and their associated predictions, such as the spectral index of primordial density perturbations and tensor-to-scalar ratio. These conditions and predictions are further analyzed to establish constraints on the models' constraints. Consequently, this review concludes by identifying the characteristics of the most feasible supergravity inflaton models.

Nonreciprocal optical systems have diverse applications that manipulate the transmission of light based on its propagation direction. This study examines a distinct class of nonreciprocity related to the correlation of photon pairs rather than the transmission of light. An experiment was conducted and supported by theoretical findings, showing this nonreciprocity through second-order coherence functions of photon pairs created by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a silicon microdisk. Changing the direction of the pump's propagation leads to significant diminishment in coherence functions while maintaining the transmission.

Superconducting quantum circuits are emerging as prominent platforms for quantum computing. For practical applications, it is essential to characterize material properties and the performance of micro-wave resonators in superconducting qubits. Traditionally, terahertz imaging has been employed to analyze terahertz radiation, a technique that can also be applied to coplanar microwave resonators despite their design limitations. By utilizing a cryogenic terahertz microscope with a gold tip, we were able to map near-field distributions within resonators, investigate their resonant states, and measure intrinsic quality factors. Furthermore, we demonstrated the technique's capability to investigate the effects of geometrical defects on superconducting qubits and explored its potential for investigating surface properties at the micro-scale in quantum devices.

We are looking for infinite cardinals $\kappa$ that allow for a division of the real number line $\mathbb R$ into $\kappa$ unique Borel sets. The well-known Hausdorff solution indicates that $\aleph_1$ sets work in one instance. Our research shows, however, that the size range for these divisions can vary extensively, allowing a specific set of natural numbers $A$ with values greater than 1 to dictate when $\aleph_\alpha$ sets work in specific instances.

In the 2000s, commodity trading advisors emerged prominently in trading, led by Richard Bookstaver, whose work is still influential today, despite the decline in their influence since then. This drop may be attributed to the entry of more competent investors into more profitable markets, influencing their returns, which can be modeled using agent-based frameworks. This study uses such models to analyze whether an investor's adoption affects market outcomes and, specifically, whether one strategy's success can undermine another, using the difference in returns, amplitude, and consistency as metrics. Simulation results indicate that although newer strategies can mitigate the initial decline in performance, they ultimately lead to a more significant decrease in returns.

Identifying the communication protocols of a network is crucial for surveillance, troubleshooting, and cybersecurity. This process becomes more complicated with dynamic protocols, whose message lengths can vary widely. A set of popular open-source tools has been developed for analyzing dynamic network traffic, but their accuracy can be compromised. This study evaluates the vulnerability of these tools to a specific type of attack designed to confuse dynamic protocol detection by altering packet order. Utilizing an automated testing framework called Fuzzing, we demonstrate that all tools under scrutiny are vulnerable to this attack. Moreover, our research reveals that current testing methods fail to sufficiently evaluate a tool's dynamic protocol detection capabilities, so we propose a new approach for effectively assessing their performance.

Electrostatic gating limits the flow of electrons in integrated circuits. Another potential means of information transfer, magnons derived from spin waves in magnetic materials, is difficult to regulate. However, we found that superconducting strips atop thin magnetic films can completely reflect magnons, producing an efficient gate. Our gate operates on the principle of the exchange interaction between magnons and Cooper pairs. The magnon gate's performance is determined by the magnetic field and Cooper pairing gap. The proposed magnon gate outperforms previous solutions, offering a novel method to control magnons and open up new possibilities for magnon-based technology.

A prominent approach in machine learning, federated learning, ensures that sensitive data remains secure and private.  The effectiveness of federated learning for well-known classes has been demonstrated in various studies, but its applicability to classes not present during training remains an unsolved challenge.  We introduce a novel problem domain, zero-shot federated learning, where a model can generalize to classes that were not encountered during training under a federated learning setup.  Focusing on audio classification as a starting point, our investigation begins with the most complex scenario of seeing new classes under a federated learning setup.  We propose two innovative techniques for enhancing generalization to new classes in audio classification: using audio features and feature extraction methods.  Experimental results on device-based federated learning platforms confirm that these strategies are effective and feasible for seeing new classes in audio classification tasks.  We also provide a comprehensive analysis of the trade-offs involved in adopting these strategies.  This research contributes to the fields of federated learning and learning with new classes in general.  The findings on achieving generalization to new classes in audio classification may have implications for other applications in a federated learning setup.

A comprehensive theoretical model is offered in this paper for analyzing high-dimensional entangled systems, specifically the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. Initially, we apply our approach to measure a complete three-photon GHZ state across three dimensions and then extend it to multi-photon systems within higher dimensional settings. In our model, both hyperentanglement of photons and the quantum Fourier transform are employed. The proposed solution will serve as a useful resource for developing high-dimensional quantum computation and communication.

This research paper delves into the problem of uplink cascaded channel estimation in multi-user multiple-input-single-output systems aided by intelligent-reflecting-surfaces. Given the immense scale of the IRS-assisted system and its associated large IRS user channel state, direct channel estimation is impractical without incurring prohibitive pilot overhead. To circumvent this limitation, we propose a two-stage compressed sensing-based estimation approach, wherein the uplink channel is decomposed into user and IRS components.
