Building upon prior work, we extend this framework to accommodate large IRS scales, leveraging the sparsity of both channels. A two-stage compressed sensing algorithm is developed to efficiently estimate each channel component separately, utilizing the respective pilot symbols, and the results show significant reductions in pilot overhead. Furthermore, simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing approaches in terms of achievable sum-rate performance.

This study analyzes data from an online monitoring system of U.S. local news to explore connections between COVID coverage, cases, deaths, and audience trends. It uses a large dataset of articles from publications representing major and minor markets, combining it with information on cases and deaths, and audience data, to investigate how these factors interact and whether local news reporting of COVID is more responsive to public health data or media consumption patterns. The study reveals that in some aspects, local news behavior aligns more with media consumption patterns than with COVID death rates, and also highlights the diversity of local news behavior, with some publications adapting more flexibly to changes in cases and deaths compared to others.

The fundamental ability to count is a universal human trait that surpasses language barriers, yet its underlying development mechanisms remain shrouded in mystery. The onset of counting skills signifies a significant cognitive milestone in children, even though they have not been exposed to the concept before. To investigate this phenomenon, we developed a neural network model that learns to count without explicit instruction. The model, incorporating a neural tower induction mechanism, demonstrates the ability to learn the concept of 'n+1' counting without direct training. Notably, our model outperforms traditional machine learning models in its capacity to generalize knowledge and even our model's performance exceeds the accuracy of children when tested on three-digit numbers. The results indicate that the simple counting ability can be effectively simulated using a universal Turing-complete computation tool without explicit concept learning.

Bloom filters provide quick approximations of set membership while consuming minimal memory. These filters help engineers prevent time-consuming operations, such as database queries, network connections, and disk access, from occurring when querying elements not in a set. Although widely used, Bloom filters have lower accuracy and a limited ability to reuse memory. In contrast, Bloom filter variants and hash-based data structures, including Cuckoo filters, have higher storage costs but offer improved approximate membership approximation. Cuckoo filters have lower reusability since only the elements not in a set can be freed. Our research introduces Xor Filters, a novel member of cuckoo filter variations that overcome these limitations, allowing for the freedom of approximate set members and providing negative bit values for bit arrays. The use of XOR operations in combining hash values reduces the need for probabilistic searches and improves accuracy to membership approximation. The results of our tests confirm that Xor Filters have lower space requirements and better accuracy than both Bloom and Cuckoo filters.

Several key connections between convex geometry and holomorphic line bundles on smooth projective varieties or K\"ahler manifolds are explored. Our investigation focuses on the relationship between positive products and mixed volumes, leading to the definition and examination of a novel addition operation for divisor classes and vector bundle classes. Specifically, we formulate a generalized version of the known convex geometry addition for divisor classes on products of projective spaces and extend the concept to arbitrary projective varieties and K\"ahler manifolds. Additionally, we investigate fundamental properties of this new addition operation, its interplay with other geometric additions, and its potential connections to higher-order convex geometry and Positively Jet bundles.

A new approach aims to derive market trend insights from dynamic price equations, specifically those that describe how future prices converge to optimal values, thereby maximizing trading volume per unit of time. We utilize historical market data from the S&P 500 Index and individual stocks, analyzing past transaction prices, quantities, and speeds, for a prediction horizon of up to two weeks into the future. The proposed methodology demonstrates moderate but positive correlation, reaching its peak at mid-term time frames, around ten days, before declining.

The popularity of distributed machine learning has led to the rise of Federated Learning (FL), a technique safeguarding user privacy during the training process. Fingerprint recognition systems depend heavily on FLVAGG, a widely-used aggregation method. However, this paper identifies critical weaknesses in FLVAGG that compromise its security and functionality, even when theoretical assumptions are met. We developed several sophisticated attacks targeting FLVAGG, verifying them through thorough theoretical analysis and experimental execution. In response, we introduced a novel aggregation strategy called $FLVoogd$, demonstrating through theoretical proofs and empirical evidence its resilience against our proposed attacks. We also evaluated $FLVoogd$ in real-world settings, showing its superior performance compared to existing alternatives, while also addressing how fingerprint databases can be compromised.

We successfully submitted the winning entry to the NeurIPS 2021 - AWS Deepracer challenge, which required developing a self-driving vehicle model that navigates a track using Sim2Real training. Sim2Real refers to the process of creating a model that operates effectively in a simulated environment and then adapts to function in a real-world setting. We developed a novel approach to simulate the transfer of a racing controller from simulation to reality by reverse-propagating image differences through gradient application. This method was combined with a model that accounts for perspective shifts and was tested on the deepracer platform, achieving top performance at the challenge.

Significant progress in deep learning technology has enabled the creation of more convincingly authentic deepfakes, which have sparked interest across multiple sectors due to their vast potential applications, despite raising serious societal and security risks. This chapter examines the advancements and difficulties in the production and identification of deepfakes, and also explores the potential solutions to improve the resilience of deepfake detection for a broad range of media, such as real-world images and videos. Furthermore, it proposes future research directions for tackling deepfake-related issues.

The orbits of sub-Neptune exoplanets are often found in similar orbits as the Earth, but their origins and structures remain unclear. The ambiguity arises from their compositions, which may be gas-dominated or consist of larger amounts of material. The existence of oceans on these exoplanets has been proposed, but their signatures are difficult to distinguish from those caused by dry atmospheres. Recent research incorporates cutting-edge modeling of chemical reactions and element solubility to analyze data from two exoplanets, GJ 3472 b and K2-18 b, considering both wet and dry scenarios. The findings suggest that analyzing the ratios of water vapor to hydrogen in these exoplanets' atmospheres using JWST may help distinguish between dry and wet compositions, particularly for GJ 3472 b and K2-18 b. The latter case might be an instance of an ocean being exposed due to atmospheric erosion, caused by a phase transition of hydrogen in mid-layers, revealing water vapor as a result.

Inspired by the classic discrete-time model of neural activity, the discrete Hopfield network, we've developed a new approach to sequence generation using a single-layer spiking neural network. By mapping discrete states to continuous vectors in a high-dimensional space, our model learns to cycle through a sequence of states via a continuous, closed trajectory that encapsulates the sequence's essence. This approach enables the network to learn complex sequences, exhibiting properties similar to human memory, such as the ability to recall incomplete or disrupted sequences and reject non-sequential inputs.

This paper reports on the findings from the 2019 Out-Of-Vocabulary challenge, where participating teams developed models to predict student grades. The specific focus was on creating effective models using training and testing data that had significant differences in vocabulary. In total, 46 entries from 13 teams took part in this challenge, with submissions being evaluated using Mean Absolute Error and Rank Correlation as key metrics. The data source for both training and testing sets was the Swedish national grade register, containing student functional and academic proficiency grades. Notably, 10 out of the 13 team entries achieved top-tier performance on the test set, indicating the complexity of handling such vocabulary discrepancies. The challenge aimed to foster the development of robust models capable of managing significant vocabulary differences between training and testing datasets, and the full data source has been made publicly available for researchers to continue exploring this area.

A specific type of chaos expansions can effectively analyze differential equations with uncertain factors by approximating random equilibrium states associated with such equations. This study integrates principles from validated calculations to provide precise error assessments alongside findings about chaos expansions representing random equilibrium states. This approach also develops a new framework for validated tracking, which entails accurately calculating separate solution branches in parameter-dependent systems and generalizes seamlessly to multi-parameter tracking. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, this research achieves the precise calculation of random equilibrium cycles in the Lorenz system, as well as solution branches and 2-dimensional planes of steady states in the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

The increased use of sensors in industrial settings has led to the widespread collection of high-dimensional data, despite this comes with its own set of difficulties. Notably, sensor failure is often accompanied by reduced data availability, rendering traditional detection methods ineffective. As a result, existing techniques either exhibit low detection accuracy exorbitant computational costs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel and adaptive sensor failure detection and isolation method. The approach leverages the non-negative matrix factorization to decompose the observation matrix into component matrices that reflect both normal and abnormal states, thereby simplifying the high-dimensional problem. The approach then utilizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence to measure the difference between the fitting observation matrix and the actual data, and defines the detection threshold to identify sensor failures. Upon detection, the algorithm employs the information theory to pinpoint the anomalous sensor through the row with the lowest mutual information. Using synthetic data and real-world data, the approach's efficacy is demonstrated, and its advantages over existing methods are showcased.

We have created a detailed formation and evolution model for dwarf galaxies, taking into account their highly variable gas outflows due to galaxy mergers and star formation. Our simulation, which uses the semi-analytic MINERVA framework, considers gas dynamics and chemical evolution, which helps us to analyze the effects of galaxy mergers on dwarf galaxy evolution. Our results show that dwarf galaxy evolution is significantly influenced by internal factors, unlike external constraints, which opens the possibility for diverse chemical development in these galaxies even with similar total galaxy mergers. However, external influences from galaxy mergers affect dwarf galaxy evolution on a larger scale, which is evident from the relationship between the dwarf galaxy's formation time and the overall baryonic efficiency during this phase. Our model also indicates that galaxy mergers affect both the overall baryonic efficiency and the efficiency of gas flows in dwarf galaxies, which is evident from the relationship between the overall baryonic efficiency and the ratio of nitrogen to oxygen in the metal products. Furthermore, we observe a variety of galaxy masses, which is consistent with the observation, and the distribution of these galaxies follows a slope that is slightly less than -1 for masses greater than $10^9$ to $10^{10}$ solar masses, which is similar to the observed pattern in the present day, and is likely a result of galaxy mergers continuing to shape these galaxies after their initial formation.

Given a profinite group G, an S[[G]]-module is a G-spectrum that fulfills certain criteria, leading to the definition of the homotopy orbit spectrum X_{hG} associated with an S[[G]]-module X. When X's constituents meet specific finiteness criteria, a homotopy orbit spectral sequence arises with an E2-term being the continuous homology of G, taking coefficients from the graded profinite \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}[[G]]-module \pi_*(X). This is demonstrated with an equivalence for certain conditions on G and Z: specifically, (Z[[G]])_{hG} is shown to be equivalent to the integral homotopy orbit spectrum of the profinite integers.

A major challenge in creating AI models that can automatically process and analyze visually complex documents such as invoices is acquiring a large, high-quality dataset to train these models. Our proposed approach, known as Selective Labeling, streamlines the labeling process by limiting the labels to simple "accept/reject" confirmations for model predictions made on partially annotated documents. This is paired with a specialized strategy for active learning, designed to identify and target model predictions with the highest levels of uncertainty. Our experiments on multiple document types across three different fields have shown that selective labeling can achieve similar extraction accuracy to a fully annotated dataset, but with significantly lower costs, specifically around a factor of 30 for our chosen examples.

The EuS/InAs interface has garnered significant interest due to its potential to exhibit quantum magnetic tunneling behavior. First principles calculations reveal that magnetic states are inherent to both InAs and EuS at this interface, with the EuS layer maintaining its cubic structure and ferromagnetic properties after bonding with InAs. The magnetization of EuS at the interface increases by 10% beyond its bulk value, primarily due to the involvement of Eu 5d states in the chemical bond with InAs. The increased magnetization can be attributed to two In site types at the interface - the first type weakly interacts with Eu, leading to a 0.15 eV energy reduction, while the second type results in a 0.6 eV0.8 eV0.8 energy reduction and the splitting of In $p$ states due to sp mixing with Eu $5f$ states. This increase in magnetization in EuS is a favorable outcome for this system.

A comprehensive classification system for subsets of Baire space, categorized by Borel Wadge classes, has been introduced with enhanced effectiveness. Based on Montalbán's true stage machinery, we leverage this innovation to offer an alternative demonstration of Louveau and Saint-Raymond's separation theorem. This leads to a demonstration of Borel Wadge determinacy within the $\text{ATR}_0+\Pi^1_1$-I system of second-order arithmetic.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have been successfully applied to a wide range of tasks, including natural language processing, image classification, and forecasting. While these applications have reached significant milestones, they often face limitations due to high latency and excessive energy consumption, particularly in resource-constrained environments. A prominent strategy to mitigate these issues has been model compression, which, however, typically focuses on inference efficiency and neglects training time optimizations. To bridge this gap, we introduce ClickTrain, a pioneering framework that enables end-to-end DNN training acceleration through fine-grained architecture preservation pruning. By exploiting the inherent patterns in neural network weights during training, ClickTrain dynamically replaces redundant operations within blocks, resulting in substantially reduced computation costs and significantly faster DNN training times, particularly for popular models like ResNet-50, GPT-2, BERT-Base, and BART-Large.

This research examines the properties of specific modal logics derived from noncommutative lattices by incorporating $\Box$ and $\Diamond$. A new semantics model is introduced, specifically tailored for substructural modal logics. By applying duality principles, we demonstrate that every modal logic derived from the full Lambek calculus has a Kripke model, if it adheres to a specific structural rule. Furthermore, we establish a dual relationship between certain mathematical structures, specifically modal algebras and topological Kripke spaces, utilizing a topological model developed from Priestley spaces.

The merging of neutron stars with black holes produces distinctive gravitational waves that hold crucial information about the events. Although traditional parameter estimation methods are highly accurate, they are computationally expensive. In contrast, using machine learning techniques for rapid detection and classification of these events can alleviate some of the strain on computational resources during future gravitational wave observatory operations. This research presents a novel approach, where we used the ResNet architecture, trained on simulated data from NEST, to automatically detect and classify NHBH mergers in the frequency domain. Our experiments demonstrate that the network achieves a notable detection rate of 98.5% and an accuracy rate of 86.5%. Furthermore, we explored the potential for using our model in a practical Bayesian analysis by combining it with the GWMC, and found that even with our limited training data, the results are comparable to those obtained from standard Bayesian methods.

A newly identified exoplanet, TOI-5542 b, was discovered using the TESS satellite and studied with data from Kepler, photometry, and radial velocity observations. The star, starlike in appearance, can be seen at a distance of 202.49 millarcseconds and has a magnitude of 14.0. It also exhibits warm characteristics with a temperature of around 4700-4800 Kelvin, indicating that it has developed convective properties. Employing Bayesian analysis and multiple radii methods, researchers have estimated TOI-5542's characteristics, including its 360.29-day orbital period, 1.7 AU distance from the star, 1.73 Jupiter masses, and 1.29 Jupiter radii, with associated uncertainties. The planet, an orbiting giant, is similar in size to Jupiter, with a significant 13-degree inclination from its star's north pole. The star, TOI-5542, is part of a rare group of G-dwarfs with metal deficiencies and lacks any companion stars, with metallicity levels much lower than our own Sun. Notably, the discovery of TOI-5542 b, along with its accompanying planet, is consistent with statistical patterns of giant exoplanets, including those detected through radial velocity and transit methods.

Sequential decision-making in operations management is addressed through the application of reinforcement learning techniques, particularly for constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs). These CMDPs enable the modeling of risk-averse policies, crucial in various fields, including aviation and healthcare. However, achieving optimal policies in constrained settings poses significant challenges due to the delicate balance between multiple objectives. To overcome these difficulties, we develop an iterative algorithm that alternates policy iteration with linear dual optimization. This approach builds upon established policy iteration principles. The convergence properties of our algorithm are analyzed and empirical evaluations demonstrate its efficiency across various CMDPs, highlighting its adaptability.

This research outlines a method for recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols when not using online recognition. The proposed system leverages a comprehensive dataset of mathematical symbols and employs offline recognition based on character segmentation. Ultimately, each extracted character is classified using a neural network. The proposed offline approach based on neural networks achieves a remarkable 97.7% success rate in recognizing mathematical symbols.

A geometric interpretation of supersymmetric quantum mechanics is developed, 
where the supercharges are defined using a superpotential function and the 
cohomology groups of the cohomology sheaves of a complex form a Hilbert space. 
The R-sector of this theory is found to describe a quantum version of the 
Cartan formula from algebraic topology, applied to complex manifolds with 
Hodge decomposition. For a specific case of a Kähler-Lie group, the Hodge 
decomposition in the R-sector matches with Hodge theory, and it is shown that 
on a torus the Hodge decomposition yields the Fock space of one-dimensional 
superqme. Moreover, for any R-sector the Hodge decomposition exceeds the 
Fock space of one-dimensional superqme.

We examine the relationship between network architecture and disease propagation in the contact process using numerical methods. Our research reveals that the diversity and complexity of network structure have a significant impact on disease variability, increasing it compared to a standard grid-based epidemic model. The irregularity of disease propagation can be influenced by the distribution of diverse network structures, such as scale-free networks, leading to unusual epidemiological outcomes despite stable overall disease levels. Next, we investigate the correlation between network architecture parameters and disease variability metrics, finding that the variance in infection duration and daily case counts can be predicted by how diseases are propagated through different network structures, influenced in part by the network's clustering characteristics.

Actor-critic reinforcement learning is a popular method for tackling Markov decision processes, yet its application often struggles with issues related to convergence and precision, which are crucial for real-world problems. Traditional actor-critic RL algorithms, utilizing parameters in policy and value functions, are prone to getting stuck in local optima and struggling with convergence. A new approach, employing the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method, eliminates policy functions in favor of state-valued functions and significantly enhances the precision of the optimal policy, particularly for tasks involving multiple steps, making it particularly effective in a variety of deep reinforcement learning tasks.

It's widely acknowledged that any prime number $p$ greater than or equal to $5$ can be represented in the form $6k \pm 1$. As consequences, Euler proved that squares of any prime number leave a remainder of 1 when divided by that prime's predecessor, leading to the pseudo-twin prime conjecture, which states that for any prime $p$ and its successor, there exists a prime between them. This implies the twin prime conjecture, based on specific conditions of composite or primality when certain arithmetic expressions are evaluated. These conclusions can also be applied to specific prime cases, such as $p = 3$.

Autonomous navigation in diverse and complex environments can pose significant challenges. However, when an environment can be decomposed into distinct layers, path planning becomes more feasible. Yet, few methods effectively utilize this layered approach for real-time navigation, especially for systems like ROVs that may rely on less accurate sonar sensors. This paper presents a technique enabling layered navigation based on the most reliable sensor data, even for sensors like sonar that typically have lower precision. By adapting the layered navigation concept, the proposed technique evaluates the reliability of multiple sensor inputs and constructs a unified map from the most accurate data for path planning. Moreover, execution relies solely on the sensor data with high correlation to the planned path for real-time navigation. This approach was tested using a COTS ROV equipped with sonar sensors, demonstrating the successful integration of the layered navigation strategy with sonar data.

Nereid, a retrograde moon of Neptune, has a diverse composition, consisting of multiple materials. Researchers analyzed Nereid's reflectance to better understand its complex surface. Contrast with other moons, such as the other two moons of Uranus, Nereid displays a distinct and varied pattern in the near-infrared spectrum. Furthermore, a significant absorption feature, Nereid shares similarities with other bodies that have a water-ice composition. Additionally, the spectral properties, Nereid exhibits a red color that is comparable to other small moons, such as those of the main belt. These spectral characteristics suggest that Nereid's surface is composed of a mixture of water-ice and other materials. Furthermore, the red color, Nereid's complex red and dark spectral properties are consistent with a surface that is not entirely water-ice. This research provides a deeper understanding of Nereid's surface composition and spectral properties.

Let $\mathcal{R}_n(q)$ be the ring of lower triangular matrices of order $n \geq 2$, consisting of elements from the finite field $F(q)$ of order $q \geq 2$. It is known that the projective line over this ring has the order $q^n$. In this paper, the conditions under which the affine line or the projective line of a ring $\mathcal{R}_n(q)$ can constitute a projective plane are investigated. Our main findings indicate that the conditions for a projective plane are met if and only if the order of the ring is either $q^2$ or $q^3$. As a direct consequence, the conditions for a projective plane of the form $A \times B$ to be met, where $A$ and $B$ are cyclic groups of order $q$, also cycle of order $q$, are determined. Furthermore, the conditions for a projective plane to be formed by the gluing of two such cycles, i.e., the semi-direct product $A \rtimes B$, i are investigated. Our results reveal that the conditions for a projective plane to be formed in these instances are the same as the cyclic case, i.e., the orders must be $q^2$ or $q^3$. These findings provide the solution to the problem of a projective plane of order $q^2$ that cannot be derived from a field of

In a 1986 paper in J. Symbolic Logic, Pawlikowski demonstrated that under specific conditions regarding Cohen and random reals, certain model properties can be inferred within extensions of those models. This is proven through a novel application of Tukey-order with models, expanding upon an existing concept introduced by Vojtáš in 1991. By leveraging this notion, it can be shown that certain model properties can imply each other, thereby establishing key theorems related to random and Cohen reals within these models.

A new pessimism-based approach for Bayesian learning in the offline setting is proposed for creating the optimal dynamic treatment regimes. Traditional offline data strategies result in sub-optimal policies due to the absence of unobserved actions, a problem that our approach tackles by training a pessimism matrix that compensates for this shortcoming. Theoretical proof confirms that our pessimism matrix can accurately reconstruct the optimal dynamic treatment regimes. The strategy is subsequently validated through simulations and a real-world analysis of the CEDAR dataset.

Dualities between subcategories of finitely generated modules over Artin algebras can be defined by the relationship to Wakamatsu tilting bimodules, with specific cases yielding known dualities. When restricting these relationships to subcategories of finitely generated modules with particular dimensions, previously established correspondences and dualities on tilting modules are reaffirmed. The implications of this relationship include demonstrating equivalences of derived categories of finitely generated Gorenstein-projective modules, as well as the invariance of certain algebraic invariants under tilting transformations.

A proposed Witzel's model for quantum theory, based on the Witzel angle, has been further examined, especially in relation to the Witzel figure. Considerations of quantum contextuality and nonlocality led to the selection of two specific complexifications of the $E_8$ root system. By calculating correlations from these complexifications, one found values that exceed those allowed by local hidden variable theories. Additionally, specific sets of measurements were determined, yielding near-maximal violations of Bell inequalities, amounting to 2.8258, which surpasses the classical limit of 2.

In a flat band with no underlying symmetry breakdown, many-body superconductivity can arise due to its inherent nature, and this phenomenon is even more prevalent when the flat band has a non-trivial topology. To study this, we develop a comprehensive approach to investigate superconducting states in topologically flat bands. Our research demonstrates that superconducting orders with both $s$-wave and p-wave symmetries are stable in a specifically designed three-dimensional band structure. The orders exhibit unique topological characteristics, which can be quantified through the Chern number and topological surface states. The resulting topological surface states display vortex patterns and can host Majorana zero modes within their vortices. The derived effective low-energy theories reveal that a topologically non-trivial parent bulk is essential for the emergence of these complex wave patterns.

The Gaussian distribution is uniquely determined by the distribution of a linear combination and a power function of independent identically distributed random variables. We identify the a-adic solenoids for which this relationship holds, effectively proving a theorem analogous to the generalized Polya theorem. This proof relies on solving a functional equation for a specific class of functions associated with the character group of the a-adic solenoid.

Presence-absence data is represented as binary vectors, reflecting the presence or absence of various entities. These vectors often come in large sets, accompanied by extensive sets of associated variables, inherently sparse, with most entries being zero, highlighting the absence of entities in most cases. To effectively analyze this data, we need to utilize suitable clustering methods, capable of handling its high dimensionality and inherent zero values. To achieve this, we develop two novel approaches, Accounting for Zeros and Weighted Distance, and through thorough simulation studies, assess their performance in complex scenarios. These simulations reveal the limitations of conventional clustering methods and the benefits of Weighted Distance and Accounting for Zeros, ultimately showcasing their superior effectiveness and establishing their superiority over existing approaches.

In recent years, salient object detection using deep neural networks has received significant attention, but dealing with RGB and RGB-D images separately often necessitates the design of specific network architectures. This paper proposes an efficient and unified structure that integrates cross-attention context extraction to effectively tackle both tasks. By effectively fusing two inputs (for RGB images) or three inputs (for RGB-D images) with a cross-attention mechanism, our framework leverages the rich information present in both RGB and depth features. This structure's simplicity and efficacy enable efficient extraction and fusion of contextual information. As shown by experimental results, our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on various datasets, including SOD, RFSOD, SBO-D, and COCOCO.

The UM-IU@LING system for the 2019 SemEval OffensEval Task is composed  of a BERT-based sentence classifier and two classifiers (SVMs) using bag-of-words features, which evaluate individual words as potentially offensive. The BERT model, fine-tuned on a subset of the target training data, predicts the most appropriate sentiment category for a given tweet. The SVMs are trained separately on white and colored subsets of words, with the "colored" subset comprising terms identified as potentially offensive by human annotators. The SVMs' predictions are then aggregated according to a predefined majority voting scheme to determine a tweet's sentiment. The BERT model is then fine-tuned on the remaining data and its predictions compared to those of the SVMs, with the BERT predictions given a weight of 2 in the weighted majority voting scheme.

A number, N, can be termed a palindrome if its binary representation reads the same forwards and backwards. In this paper, we explore two collections of numbers, derived from symmetric (palindromic) and antisymmetric (antipalindromic) properties of their binary representations, separated by a midpoint. We analyze all possible ratios of N/S (N being a natural number, S a palindrome/antipalindromic number) in terms of a partition scheme, demonstrating that each partition has both a minimum and maximum limit. Ultimately, we compute the sets of all possible values for N/S within these minimum and maximum bounds for each partition.

Computed tomography (CT) reconstruction from multiple polyenergetic sources allows for the determination of additional information beyond standard CT data, such as material properties, but this process is hindered by noisy data and limited measurements, resulting in an underdetermined problem. To address these challenges, we have developed a novel reconstruction model that combines source-specific data with two previously established variational frameworks, enabling simultaneous reconstruction of common, individual, and detection matrices, followed by a further separation of the common matrix into distinct material densities. The underlying variational model is non-convex, which we address using alternating minimization. Our approach also utilizes specialized algorithms for the reconstruction and decomposition processes. Our method's effectiveness is demonstrated through extensive numerical experiments using realistic synthetic data, showing its superior performance compared to a competing approach.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) with limited resources is a complex task, 
particularly in languages that are less commonly used. The absence of extensive 
keyboard data hinders the learning process, making it essential to develop innovative 
approaches. This paper presents a data augmentation technique based on a compositional 
model. It outlines the requirements for decomposing the handwriting sample space 
and generating synthetic datasets from basic elements. This method enables the 
creation of virtual datasets utilizing only a single handwritten specimen per 
character class, eliminating the need for multilingual samples. The study examines 
how synthetic data compares to human-annotated labels in terms of performance. 
We utilize the Basic Coptic script as a case study, demonstrating that our approach 
yieldes results nearly comparable to those of a fully annotated dataset.

We have developed a novel computational framework that enables precise energy and
structural properties of superheavy elements to be computed with high efficiency.
This framework integrates a sophisticated single-particle model based on a tailored
Woods-Saxon potential with 26 major levels and a comprehensive residual interaction
matrix, allowing efficient calculation of the effects of nucleon interactions.
Our calculations, which cover all even-even nuclei beginning from BiBi and extending
through the periodic table up to ZrSr, demonstrate remarkable agreement between
predicted values and experimental data for binding energy and nuclear mass.
The root-mean-square error relative to the experimental values is only 0.55 MeV.
Furthermore, the error relative to the latest nuclear mass models is comparable, at
0.44 MeV. The framework precisely predicts the numbers of low-lying excited states
in heavy nuclei and their corresponding energy levels, correctly identifying the
nature of these excitations. The framework's proficiency in computing nuclear
properties has enabled a novel discovery in the domain of heavy nuclei, specifically
the identification of a 'island of stability' extending as far as the element with
atomic number ZrSr. The island includes several previously unknown nuclei: a line
of neutron magic nuclei: ZrSr, and it also includes other stable nuclei: RnPo, and it also includes LvTs.

We invite undergraduate students and early graduate students to an educational introduction to one-dimensional topological phases, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. This will include discussions on entanglement using the correlator method and von Neumann density matrix, as well as geometric phase, polarization, and transport characteristics, all with consideration of electron-electron interactions. Hands-on numerical experiments guided by publicly available codes are used to convey the value of using topological toy models for exploring new concepts in quantum electronics.

This study examines the compactness of composition operators within Bergman spaces associated with bounded, convex domains in complex n-dimensional space. It also investigates compactness in areas linked to specific types of complex curves.

We derived a two-loop amplitude formula for four graviton supermultiplets in AdS$_5$ times S$^5$ using a pre-amplitude representation and the unique structure of on-shell graph amplitlets. The derived formula aligns with the two-loop four particle multipoint amplitude in flat space and can be applied to evaluate multipoint amplitlets for various CFT data extraction purposes.

High-performance computing on massive GPU arrays is hampered by inefficient memory management in GPU programming, which hampers the adoption of arrays in object-oriented programming. To address this issue, high-level languages like Fortran and Python utilize a memory manager called GDRFA to handle memory in GPU arrays, but this limits the potential of exploiting the entire GPU memory space. This research presents DynaSOAr, an object-oriented memory manager that operates independently of the host, capable of allocating memory for objects, including those stored on GPU arrays, in languages like Python and C++. DynaSOAr is particularly effective in maximizing the use of hierarchical memory spaces and executing high-latency memory operations in parallel, outperforming the built-in GPU memory manager, and facilitating the development of GPU-based high-level language software, including Python, by 1.77 times.

We introduce and study generic $U(1)_X$ models based on the $SO(10)$ GUT group, with the group $U(1)_X$ being a generic linear combination of B-L and $U(1)_{\Delta L_\alpha}$ where $\alpha$ represents the electron, muon, or tau lepton number. A general $U(1)_X$ model is characterized by its simplicity and universality, featuring the Standard Model as a subgroup of $U(1)_X \times U(1)_Y$ or $U(1)_X \times U(1)_W$ and incorporating only two additional fermion doublets in the context of $SO(10)$. Our analysis specifically examines the generic $U(1)_X$ model consisting of $SO(10)$ with right-handed neutrinos and two additional fermion doublets, denoted as $16 \times 2$, and labeled as Model G, where $U(1)_X$ corresponds to a linear combination of B-L and $U(1)_{\Delta L_\alpha}$ with positive coefficients, analyzed through collider and low-energy phenomenology.

A specific measurement technique must be used for assessing the mechanical characteristics of straw tubes designed for charged particle detection, operating in a vacuum environment. The underlying equations that govern straw behavior when subjected to internal pressure are documented, alongside the introduction of new experimental data obtained from 2 mm and 3 mm diameter fiberglass-fibred glasses, circular tubes subjected to internal pressure. The tests, conducted using a loading frame, involved measuring the tubes' response under incremental pressure increments while monitoring the tube's surface for deformation. The experiments revealed the tubes' mechanical limits before failure, revealing that 2 mm and 3 mm diameter fibers glasses could withstand pressure levels comparable to those used in the LHC. The provided data on mechanical properties can serve as a reference for engineers designing detectors that utilize straw tubes.

In many cases, machine learning models are trained under the assumption that training and testing data come from the same distribution, which is often not the case in practice. When data is subject to subtle shifts, such as changes in lighting, angle, or font, the performance of these models can be severely compromised, leading to significant performance drops. Addressing this issue, we introduce a framework for measuring how robust trained models are to subtle distribution changes, with a particular focus on credal Bayesian networks. At the heart of our approach is the concept of epsilon-contamination, which measures the maximum level of adversarial manipulation of a distribution that a model can tolerate. Advancing existing research, we expand the range of possible values for epsilon, and achieve this by formulating the problem as a constraint optimization issue on probabilistic circuits. Since this problem is NP-hard, we propose two innovative solutions: a simplified version of the optimization issue and an iterative algorithm based on duality theory. Experimental results show that our methods effectively and accurately estimate the robustness of credal Bayesian networks on a variety of tabular datasets, with the process being computationally feasible.

In a supersolid Bose-Einstein condensate with a spin-orbit coupling, an accelerated impurity atom exhibits oscillations that mirror Bloch oscillations in solid matter, despite causing condensate excitements that affect the oscillation frequency, which also depends on the coupling between the impurity and the condensate.

In a generalised quadrangle, a code is a subset of the vertices with its minimum distance determined by the smallest separation between distinct points and the code. If the minimum distance is seven, it is known as a code with parameter seven. Neighbour-7-transitive codes with quadrangle structure have specific dot product properties. The main goal of this study is to demonstrate that such codes generate partial spreads in certain types of quadrangles, specifically of types GD and XY, except for one instance. To achieve this, we employ linear algebra techniques in conjunction with computational verification. Consequently, our findings imply the validity of the quadrangle conjecture for types GD and the validity of the Neighbour-7-transitive conjecture for the D4 graph type.

Located at the heart of the Milky Way lies the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ), a distinct ring-like formation, where analysis of the 870 $\mu$m continuum map from ATLASGAL, obtained via the APEX Telescope Large Area Survey of the Galaxy, revealed notable anisotropy in gas density within this area using a two-dimensional correlation function. By applying this statistical tool, the most prevalent orientation of the ring was identified at a 65 degree position with high confidence levels of 95-99%. Furthermore, the mean fractional standard deviation of the two-dimensional correlation function demonstrated a fractional decrease of up to 30-40%, facilitating more precise identification of the CMZ's ring-like structure with a 50% reduction in angular resolution. This research also highlights the efficacy of this technique in identifying cosmic structures across various frequency bands and with lower angular resolution.

Scientists have proposed the plasmon model to interpret x-ray absorption near edge spectra (XANES) following core electron excitation. This plasmon model relies on solving a set of differential equations that track the population of electronic states. In this research, we apply the plasmon model to simulate L_3-edge XANES of vanadium using the codes implemented in the FHI-aims code, focusing on its response to single and multiple pump-probe x-ray pulses. After obtaining plasmon width values from single pulse simulations, we utilize these values to simulate plasmon oscillations, which we compare to experiment to infer the nonequilibrium carrier temperature. In nonequilibrium conditions, we observe disparate nonequilibrium lifetimes for different electronic states, a result inconsistent with the assumptions used in conventional XANES data analysis.

This research introduces a new sub-threshold current-based temperature sensing technique that builds upon the concept of a difference in sub-threshold voltage over drive current, contributing to lower power consumption. The proposed method involves measuring the ratio of sub-threshold currents from nMOS and pMOS transistors, each with dimensions scaled according to their respective threshold currents, resulting in a substantial difference in drive currents. The transistor sizes were carefully chosen based on sub-threshold conduction principles to ensure the maximal difference in their drain currents, ultimately leading to improved efficiency and an output that is directly proportional to the absolute temperature. The proposed sensor architecture features a carefully designed resistor network to minimize area and consume minimal power, achieved through the careful selection of supply voltage levels and transistor sizes, which directly influence the output current. This design enables greater output swing and facilitates easier level shifting. The proposed sensor's performance was rigorously evaluated through 180nm CMOS implementation, utilizing SPICE simulations to validate its efficacy. The proposed scheme demonstrated a 99.9%\% range linearity and exceptional power efficiency, yielding an energy per conversion of 1.06nJ. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits an impressive 0.24{\deg}C resolution and \pm1.4{\deg}C inaccuracy.

Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information theory and a crucial resource for quantum information processing, can only be achieved through interactions between non-classical states. Following its discovery as a consequence of wave-like behavior, entanglement has been generated in various ways. Here, we present a novel approach to entanglement generation that relies on wave properties rather than conflating momenta. Our scheme, analogous to swapping moments, is based on a quantum scissors method that enables the creation of a specific polarization entangled state of single photons, guaranteed by a preceding measurement. We successfully generated entangled photons with the assistance of a classical resource, and this method offers advantages for creating high-photon-count entangled states applicable to optical quantum information processing.

This paper explores the concept of online Euclidean spanners in the geometric online setting. A geometric online problem is considered when the objective function depends on the points of a set that grows over time. For a given geometric optimization problem, we define a pointset Euclidean $c$-spanner as an arrangement of lines and curves in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that encompasses the given points, expands distances by at most a factor of $c$, and minimizes its complexity. We focus on two applications: the online Euclidean traveling salesman problem and the online Euclidean clique cover problem. We propose an algorithm for the geometric online problems that produces arrangements with suboptimal factors of $c$, with a complexity of $O(nc)$ and a cost of $O(n^{1-1/k}c^{1/(k-1)})$. Additionally, we provide lower bounds on the cost for these problems.

Accurate categorization of IoT devices is vital for safeguarding them against cyber threats. To facilitate this, we develop an economic efficiency framework for selecting device characteristics that minimize the cost associated with monitoring or attacking them. The proposed system utilizes binary classification on a subset of available features to maximize the trade-off between precision, recall and monitoring costs, a framework we term the Feature Per-Autoencoder (FaPA). Our approach addresses the challenge associated with sparse data and high dimensionality by reducing it to its most effective feature space using autoencoders and cost-based selection. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that FaPA achieves significant improvements over traditional feature selection methods.

Godel modal logics can be regarded as an extension of intutionistic modal logics with prelinearity. This study explores relational semantics for Godel modal logics, building on the work of Escher and Czelakowski. The authors define algebraic and relational models for Godel modal logics, demonstrating that prelinearity is essential for the soundness and completeness of the logic. The study then examines specific examples of Godel modal logics, including the Kripke semantics for the three-valued S4 logic introduced by Czelakowski. By applying algebraic and relational models to these logics, the authors show that certain prelinear extensions of substructural logics have prelinear Herbrand models, thus providing a positive answer to the strong completeness of the three-valued S4.

This research presents a novel and straightforward technique for word-alignment that leverages bilingual information from external sources like machine translation platforms. We demonstrate that a model with limited parameters can achieve performance comparable to GIZA++ when trained on a relatively small dataset, potentially on a corpus as small as 1,000 parallel sentences. Notably, even with a significantly larger training dataset of 100,000 sentences, our model maintains an accuracy of 77.77%, very close to the 78.63% achieved by GIZA++ on the same data, indicating the model's robustness. Furthermore, our findings reveal that incorporating low-frequency high-level alignments through external bilingual resources substantially boosts the model's performance. This approach's versatility and ease of implementation make it suitable for integration within existing pipelines, including those for morphological processing and machine translation, where dynamic word alignment is feasible and advantageous.

We suggest an asynchronous algorithm to solve Nash equilibrium problems by iteratively decomposing them into simpler optimization tasks called subproblems. These subproblems can be solved using the Accelerated Proximal Gradient method, taking advantage of the problem's resolvent structure. Inspired by Warped Gradient Descent, our algorithm is named Warped Proximal Gradient and it relies on carefully crafted weights for each player, which also yield variational characterizations of the original Nash equilibrium problem. The method's properties are also examined within the context of variational analysis.

The theoretical primordial black holes formed in the early universe are a potential candidate for explaining dark matter. If they account for all the dark matter in the universe, their effects on the population of neutron stars and black holes formed later would be noticeable. If PopSyCLE's current model incorporating PR3 is accurate, then the existence of primordial black holes as dark matter would significantly alter the predicted number of neutron stars and black holes detected by LIGO and Virgo, particularly in the 10 to 30 solar masses range.

We conducted research on systems of homomolecular, hard-chain-like molecules using Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on their properties in the regime of high density and low temperature, in containers shaped as square, hexagonal, and hexagonal with ridges. The molecules in the systems resembled actual chain-like molecules in that they had significant potential for different arrangements, or phasing, within their containers. Our study revealed the existence of various phase states, including solid, liquid, and perhaps a second liquid state, in the systems we examined. Furthermore, we discovered that one of the system's characteristics influenced the existence of these phase states and their transitions. This characteristic was the number of molecular units included in the molecular molecules, denoted as N. Based on our results, we found that the systems consisting of three molecular units (N=3) had no transitional phase states, whereas those with two (N=2) and four (N=4) molecular units exhibited clear transitions between different phase states.

Recurrences in positive definite functions, especially concerning the underlying space dimension, have been widely utilized in various applications. These recurrences are often linked to the geometry of the generation process, especially when the spatial structure is represented on a spherical surface. The recurrences on the sphere are commonly associated with the addition theorem of solid harmonics, leading to the widespread acceptance of the use of Gegenbauer polynomials as a model for spherical random fields. The present study derives new sets of one-step recurrences for stationary random fields defined on the sphere and demonstrates how the new sets, particularly those involving Gegenbauer polynomials, are related to the implicit positive definiteness of certain matrices. The work also includes discussions on implicit positive definiteness and their applications to random fields.

A conventional imaging scenario relies on measuring light that has both traveled to and returned from the subject. However, we have developed a quantum imaging technique that makes it possible to image without detecting the light that has interacted with the subject. A single-pixel imaging method is used, which utilizes a pair of entangled photons, where the signal photon's presence is determined by the idler photon. By utilizing near-field spatial correlations and the interference of photon signals, high-resolution images of objects can be reconstructed despite the absence of interaction between the subject and the light. This research offers a promising pathway for the development of near-field imaging technologies in challenging environments.

The flow of complex liquids is significantly influenced by surface roughness, especially at interfaces. Through the use of experiments and theoretical models, the effects of surface roughness on dry friction in deformable foams has been investigated. The experiments involve a glass plate and a foam, with the plate being moved back and forth while the other plate remains stationary. The plate that is not fixed covers the interface, resembling a bubble, whose internal pressure is represented by the stress on the interface. The movement of the plate is recorded along with the force it takes to move the interface. The relationship between the roughness and the force is observed to resemble a static friction model where the force required to move the interface increases with roughness, however the exponent in this relationship is observed to decrease with increased strain rate. The study reveals that the stress in the foam plays a major role in the stress roughness relationship, with the stress influencing the stress roughness exponent through the stress tensor's influence on the foam structure, with the stress tensor's influence on the foam structure, with the stress tensor's influence on the foam structure, with the stress tensor's influence on the foam structure

This paper introduces an advanced deep learning framework for accurate skin cancer
identification from dermoscopic images. The proposed framework utilizes a deep
convolutional neural network to automatically extract distinctive features from the
images, which are then used to improve cancer detection performance. A novel outlier
detection technique employing the maximum principle is proposed to identify anomalous
images that could negatively impact performance. The framework achieves a superior
performance of 96.44% in evaluating accuracy on the ISIC 2017 challenge dataset.

We carried out a high-resolution ARPES study on sodium and found that the observed enhancement of its electronic mass is slightly less than expected from earlier research. These findings amplify the need for theoretical models more advanced than the random phase approximation. Contrary to the hypothesis suggesting significant acceleration of the carriers due to their interaction with spin fluctuations, our results do not support this theory. Additionally, a comparison with previous electron loss data indicates that sodium's mass enhancement due to dipole-type electron-hole interactions is substantially less than its mass enhancement due to monopole-type interactions measured using ARPES.

We derive an equation for calculating how the volume of the phase space is modified when a system undergoes a structural change. This equation is then used to track the evolution of $q_1, p_1$ Hamiltonian system trajectories. We apply our findings to a free expansion process of a two-dimensional gas, where a barrier within a container is suddenly removed. By comparing the calculated and measured volumes of the phase space before and after the expansion, we verify our results to within a margin of error of 0.0006%.

This passage provides an in-depth, explicit calculation for the weights of Kontsevich graphs that emerge from connections and curvatures within a symplectic manifold framework, specifically focusing on globalization. We demonstrate that curvature graph weights can be explicitly defined through a hypergeometric function and, in certain cases, expressed as a combination of logarithms of rational numbers. Our investigation also examines generalizations of these findings to higher degrees of curvature.

We explore solitary waves in the woodpile chain and the diatomic chain subjected to small nonlinear forces beyond the threshold of the linear regime. These models, consisting of spherical masses connected to massless springs, are subject to linear damping and external driving powered by the undamped natural frequency. We discover that solitary waves emerge from the intersection of two key frequencies: one derived from the undamped natural frequency and the other from the driving frequency and the damping rate of the woodpile chain and a specific branch of the diatomic chain's spectrum. The amplitude of these waves is controlled by the difference between these frequencies and decays exponentially with the square of the distance between them. As a result, the solitary waves exhibit narrow spatial features.

Extra signals hidden in the nonlinear structure of the cosmos may reveal the existence of heavy particles linked to primordial fluctuations. These signals are encoded in the correlations of tensor and helicity modes produced by primordial features. Features that modify the spectrum of tensor fluctuations can leave a distinctive imprint on the tensor mode non-Gaussianity. We investigate the imprint features leave on the three-point correlation function of tensor modes within specific scenarios, including a case where features create a local enhancement in tensor power spectrum, a case where features create a bubble of compressive gravitational waves, as well as features that generate a loop of compressive gravitational waves. We demonstrate that features can induce a three-point correlation signal characterized by an eight-fold asymmetry. We derive a universal expression for the tensor mode non-Gaussianity across these scenarios, and our findings have substantial implications for the development of the Cosmological Collider.

Consider a graph of even order that is vertex-transitive and has a valence of four or greater, and let's denote the set of edges that do not connect opposite vertices as E*. Our main finding indicates that the large cycle factor number, denoted by gf(G), of an "accordion graph" G is equal to 2, which means that every matching in G can be expanded into a set of two disjoint matchings. Furthermore, we demonstrate that G is isomorphic to the circulant graph Gi(φ, d, n) under the condition that its large cycle factor number is equal to 2. To achieve this, we introduce an explicit mapping that shows the relationship between I(φ, d, n) and G.

We carry out a finite-time scaling analysis near the detrapping point in a three-state quantum walk model. The coin operator is adjusted using parameter $\rho$ that controls the speed of wavepacket dispersion. The initial wavefunction is a symmetric superposition of two adjacent basis states. Contrary to previous studies on two-state models, in the three-state model, the wavefunction's first moment behaves asymmetrically. Furthermore, the wavefunction's higher odd moments show finite-size scaling behavior, but their temporal evolution remains size-independent. The generalized dynamical scaling exponents for the $k$-th moment, denoted as $\beta_k$, $\nu_k$, and $\alpha_k$, are found. It is found that in the limit of large $\rho$, the scaling exponents for the $k$-th moment in the three-state model converge to those of the one-dimensional free-particle system.

This research delves into the characteristics of self-supervised vision transformers (SVTs), addressing a significant knowledge gap. Unlike supervised classifiers, which incorporate human-provided labels, SVT is unhampered by the need to label vast datasets, yet supervised knowledge distillation has proven effective in guiding network training. However, supervised knowledge distillation is not applicable to SVT, as it relies on a student model with inferior performance. To bridge this knowledge gap, our study explores the potential of supervised tasks as pretraining objectives for student models, as this can yield beneficial results. Moreover, we investigate how supervised tasks can compress the intrinsic representations of SVT. Experimental findings demonstrate that supervised characteristics can be efficiently induced and integrated into SVT without degrading its unsupervised performance. Moreover, we leverage these supervised characteristics to enhance the switchability and small-scale robustness of SVT. Ultimately, our study establishes self-supervised vision transformers as a robust backbone for visual pattern recognition.

A unified dark fluid model of a Bardeen-Like type has been developed that combines dissipative effects with the combination of dark energy and dark matter. This fluid model has been extensively analyzed by employing a time-dependent quantitative method to demonstrate its feasibility. A newly created dissipation coefficient with two distinct regimes - one showing a quadratic dependence on time and the other dependent on the inverse of time - has been used to study the behavior of the model under different conditions. It has been proven that this model behaves as an adiabatic fluid in the adiabatic limit, whereas it behaves as a quasi-static fluid when the quasi-static limit is applied. By applying the two regimes, it has been demonstrated that these conditions yield截然相反的 behavior, thus the significance of both time's past and future is highlighted. Furthermore, stability analysis has been performed using a standard perturbation technique resulting in complex roots, thus the model cannot serve as a fluid description of a cosmic fluid.

We present a straightforward proof that in three or more dimensions, the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations has a critical issue in terms of stability, specifically when using Sobolev spaces and certain types of Lorentz spaces, thereby confirming an earlier study by Bourgain and Li.

Recently, large text-conditioned generative diffusion models have revolutionized the creation of high-quality synthetic media, however, the inability to precisely control the generated images remains a significant challenge.  Proposed diffusion guidance techniques enable some degree of control, mostly by post-processing or adjusting the model's output distribution, yet they ignore the guidance provided during the training phase.  We present the first study exploring the concept of conditional guidance in diffusion models, introducing the Stable Artist framework.  Stable Artist allows users to define and customize semantic attributes for individual images during training, rendering it possible to change the attributes of existing images simply by modifying specific tags without the need for additional training.  Stable Artist framework excels in generating high-quality images that accurately reflect requested attributes compared to other methods.  Furthermore, we demonstrate its exceptional capability to not only increase the attributes desired in an image but also decrease attributes undesired, opening up a broad range of applications for image manipulation and customization.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have accelerated its adoption, but the integration of reversible steganography remains a challenging issue, as traditional methods either fail to preserve image quality or fail to maintain data confidentiality. Our research focuses on addressing this gap by leveraging Bayesian reasoning and deep learning. A probabilistic approach is adopted to model signal statistics using Bayesian Neural Networks, and the results demonstrate its superiority over alternative methods in maintaining image quality and keeping secret data confidential. Moreover, our method outperforms competing solutions in various tests and applications, and enables the extraction of secret information even when the host image is altered.

Our research investigates the implications of the J/ψ particle decaying into invisible matter for light neutral neutrinos and dark matter. In conjunction with existing studies, we utilize the observed limitation on J/ψ decays into visible matter and one or two photons to constrain the properties of neutrino and dark matter effective field theories. Specifically, we focus on the limitations imposed by these constraints on two-neutrino production along with dark matter and a photon, as well as one neutrino, a photon, and a dark matter particle. By analyzing collider data, our study expands the accessible range for determining the coefficients and mass scales of neutrino effective field theories to include lower mass scales than previously possible using terrestrial facilities. Furthermore, the data significantly refines the limits on certain dark matter effective field theories involving light quarks, essentially eliminating mass scales below the square of five TeV for odd and below 10 TeV for even dark matter mass cases.

High-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal tiny magnetic bright points, associated with extremely strong magnetic fields, present in numerous simulations of the solar atmosphere. These features are crucial in the solar energy balance, as they contribute significantly to the quiet Sun's radiative emission and may be responsible for observed heat in its chromosphere. Despite their importance, observational evidence for magnetic bright points has been scarce, as most previous studies were limited by the resolution of available instruments. These shortcomings were addressed in this research, which analyzed 3442 magnetic bright points identified in high-fidelity synthetic images of the solar photosphere, produced by extensive Magnetohydrodynamic simulations. These simulations were used to train an artificial intelligence, which then identified magnetic bright points in new synthetic images. By doing so, this research provided the first direct comparison of the properties of magnetic bright points, as determined by simulations, with the same properties of another type of solar feature, granulation, which were both analyzed through the same machine learning framework. By comparing these two features, this research revealed distinct distributions of their temperatures and magnetic field strengths, indicating that the magnetic bright points have significantly higher temperatures and significantly weaker magnetic field strengths, as opposed to the granulation. These findings suggest that the standard model of the solar atmosphere, which relies heavily on magnetic bright points to explain the solar energy balance, may be inaccurate, as the observed characteristics of these features do not match the predicted distributions, as required by this theoretical framework.

Human vision can distinguish objects and actions using spatial or temporal data, but integrating these aspects remains unclear. This study demonstrates how the human visual system can effectively combine spatial and motion information, enabling recognition in scenarios where individual sources are insufficient. Researchers achieved this insight by analyzing'minimal videos' - brief clips that facilitate reliable object, part, and action recognition, but are unrecognizable when spatial or temporal constraints are compromised. Unlike existing deep networks, humans exhibit more adept performance in these complex configurations, highlighting missing dynamic vision mechanisms in current models.

Dark particles that exhibit magnetic charge and dynamic responses to galactic magnetic fields might serve as a source of magnetic energy in our galaxy, potentially altering the magnetic fields we observe today. Using a dark matter model that embodies dual properties, we investigate how monopoles contribute to the magnetic energy evolution in the Milky Way's disk as a fluid. The efficiency of this energy conversion is significantly influenced by the distribution of dark matter within the galaxy, a factor heavily dependent on galactic magnetic field observations, particle properties, and simulation outcomes. The research suggests that if the dark matter particle is composed of a bound state of dark quarks with a mass of less than 100 MeV, it would undermine the magnetic fields in the Milky way, implying that monopole dark matter is incompatible with models predicting a metastable dark matter state formed from a confined quantum field.

The objective of statistical weather forecasting is to predict future weather patterns based on historical weather data, aiding decision-making processes. This study introduces a new two-stage deep learning model, combining transformer and convolutional techniques. The initial stage, an encoder, utilizes multiple transformers to encode initial meteorological data and identify crucial features for forecasting. A decoder then applies a real-time forecasting mechanism using stacked 2D convolutions. To address the limitations of long-range dependency in traditional CNNs, the encoder leveraged transformers. Due to the computational expense of self-attention in transformers, particularly on high-resolution images, the framework incorporates shifted window-based cross-attention. Furthermore, the study evaluates and compares various weather indicator selection methods, and the results demonstrate the proposed framework's superior performance on the Weather42 dataset for two hours ahead forecasting.

In models that incorporate multiple Higgs fields, such as a triplet, there is an opportunity to link them to dark matter through symmetry-based interactions, which can also yield detectable signals through the LHC and various dark matter search experiments. A specific type of model, based on the $S_3$ symmetry and constrained by electroweak rules, has been analyzed in terms of its possible connections to dark matter. By classifying the models according to their global symmetry, we find two scenarios where dark matter exists, with one scenario featuring zero mass differences between the scalar particles, leading to unique outcomes. Furthermore, we examine the conditions for stable dark matter and determine its possible nature, with potential implications for collider experiments and dark matter searches.

A comprehensive study on the PPT square conjecture is presented with a notable achievement: the PPT square conjecture's validity has been rigorously demonstrated for the case involving finite-dimensional space.

Intracellular traffic congestion hinders the delivery of vital substances to critical areas of the cell, including the axon terminal. The current research aims to model and analyze a local mechanism that controls and optimizes the transportation of materials within the cell. An optimal transport system is established to maximize the delivery of essential substances to the axon terminal while minimizing the formation of traffic jams. The optimization problem involves solving partial differential equations to determine the optimal distribution of materials, as well as a constrained optimization problem to find the optimal parameters. The study reveals the existence of a steady-state and provides a closed-form expression for the optimal distribution of materials, as well as the optimal parameters of the control system. The research demonstrates the stability and convergence of the optimal parameters, as well as the existence of a feedback-controlled system that generates traffic jams in the axon. The results of this study demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimal transport system in generating traffic jams, while also ensuring the stability and convergence of the traffic patterns. The traffic patterns exhibit damped oscillations and converge to a steady-state distribution, characterized by a non-zero, measure-zero set of points. The steady-state distribution consists of a finite set of non-zero, exponentially decreasing components and a infinite set of components that converge to zero. The traffic patterns within the axon exhibit a unique, optimal distribution that generates traffic jams, as well as a unique, optimal parameter that generates a specific type of traffic jam, as well as a unique, optimal parameter that generates a specific

Billion-dollar losses inflicted by banking fraud across the globe make graph-based fraud detection in transactions increasingly significant. In analyzing transaction patterns, researchers utilize graphs to identify novel and complex schemes. This research aims to identify real-world transaction network patterns, specifically network motifs within a heterogenous transaction graph. We also present a method for generating genuine banking transaction graphs via randomization. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated by detecting a predefined network motif in genuine banking graphs that correlates with increased transaction volumes and key hubs. Additionally, our results indicate that certain nodes exhibiting exceptional network motif activity may be linked to significant financial losses and key figures within organizations.

In a black hole-white dwarf binary system, we examine electromagnetic and gravitational waves emitted during a process where a white dwarf loses mass to a black hole through tidal forces. We simulate this scenario using a quantum hydrodynamic model and represent the white dwarf as a zero-temperature Bose-Fermi droplet. When the white dwarf approaches its point of black hole disruption, it undergoes a transition to the black hole's accretion disk, resulting in the release of energetic electromagnetic and gravitational waves. These waves can be detected by future observatories, KNOM and LISA, potentially offering new insights into the unique physics governing mass transfer in these systems.

Three-body $\tau$ decays, which are semileptonic processes with momentum transfer dependence, are sensitive to both the hadronic current and form factors, which can be affected by physics beyond the standard model. A comprehensive method, which can also test the SM and BSM hypotheses via three-body differential rates, is proposed to analyze these dependencies.

We establish a parametric overview of the Tversky similarity function's generalized distance, in relation to the Jaccard distance. The review also establishes the distance's non-negative, symmetric, and triangle inequality properties. The parameters that yield the Jaccard distance are shown to be the limiting case of the broader Tversky metric. Furthermore, the review identifies all Tversky metrics distances and demonstrates the complete set encompasses both the normalized and non-normalized variants. An illustrative application of the analysis is provided, utilizing human-generated binary vectors to showcase the relationships between the different distance measures.

Modern motion deblurring methods based on deep learning utilize paired blurry and sharp images for training, however, these approaches face challenges due to the scarcity of sharp images and the difficulties in evaluating performance. The proposed solution tackles these issues by employing a pseudo-blurring technique, generating an unlimited supply of sharp human and scene images, and providing vast amounts of blurry and corresponding images, thereby facilitating the development of motion deblurring methods. The evaluation of this pseudo-blurring method also reveals current limitations in motion deblurring methods. The proposed approach serves as a valuable tool for the continued advancement of motion deblurring.

Neuromorphic computing aims to develop neural networks by using custom hardware that mimics the human brain, incorporating specialized neural processors and alternative materials. Similarly, molecular neuromorphic computing seeks to achieve this goal by leveraging molecular properties. Building on a recent breakthrough where a custom circuit emulated a known biological neuron model, we have taken a significant step forward by creating a novel approach to neural computation that emulates a complex learning neuron, emulating the NMDA receptor. This groundbreaking approach, for the first time, captures the neural network's ability to remember past experiences. We have successfully demonstrated its practicality by integrating the custom molecular component into a circuit designed to mimic the cellular mechanism underlying a key brain disease, epilepsy. We anticipate this innovative strategy will pave the way for the development of new neural systems, potentially leading to the creation of artificial brains with unprecedented capabilities.

The ultrapower of any ordered set is created as a refined version of the set itself by taking into account infinite sequences of elements from it. This process involves dividing the sequences into classes according to a set of rules defined by an ultrafilter, leading to a set that always satisfies a fundamental property of ordered sets. It turns out that a set's openness determines its ability to fulfill the open completeness property in the refined version, whereas its original cardinality dictates whether the refined version is complete.

Scientific progress in data science is largely driven by benchmark datasets, 
whose quality issues can substantially hinder advancement. While profiling 
techniques facilitate the detection of dataset characteristics, they are usually
